viewpoints.translatedContent: 代码之所以非常适合智能体处理，其中一个重要特性是你可以相对快速地对其进行测试。你可以手动检查应用程序是否正常运行，也可以直接对你构建的内容运行测试。而大多数其他工作领域则不具备这种优势。只有当最终产品以某种形式投入实际应用时——比如执行股票交易、谈判合同、进行销售推介等——你才能获得测试反馈。关于如何以这种方式开始测试其他类型的工作，很可能会涌现出一系列全新的机遇。最终，这将意味着更多智能体被融入工作流程中。同时，这也意味着我们需要对大多数工作流程进行更完善的评估。如今，企业中的大部分工作都没有相应的评估机制，无法判断模型、提示或系统变更是否导致了问题或改进。那些能够最有效评估其知识工作的企业，也将从人工智能中获得最大收益。随着时间的推移，这将成为智能体普及的关键因素。
viewpoints.originalContent: One of the many properties that code has that makes it highly amenable to agents is that you can more or less quickly test it. You can either go see if the application works manually, or you can actually run a test on what you built. Most other areas of work don’t have this benefit. You only get the testing when the final product hits the real world in some capacity - a stock trade is executed, a contract is negotiated, a sales pitch is delivered, and so on. There’s probably going to be a whole new set of opportunities for how we begin to test the rest of work in this way. Ultimately it will mean more agents being layered into workflows. It also means we need much better evals on most of our workflows. Most work today in enterprises doesn’t have an associated eval to know if something broke or improved with a model, prompt, or system change. The enterprises that are able to eval their knowledge work the best also stand to gain the most from AI. Will become a critical aspect of agent adoption over time.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 当梦想成为工作 我曾以为，梦想就是把爱好变成工作。 用一生去靠近那些我热爱的事物： 电脑、工具、界面、系统、微小的细节， 那种从无到有创造东西的感觉。 那些曾经在夜晚、放学后、下班后、在生活缝隙里做的事， 不知怎的，成了我生活的中心。 这确实是一个梦想。我不想假装不是。 有一种很具体的幸福， 在于有人付钱让你去在乎。 在于遇见其他也在乎的人。 在于围绕你的痴迷构建一套语言。 在于看到只存在于你脑海中的东西，变得足够真实，让别人也能触碰。 但其中也藏着一种安静的痛苦。 因为那件曾经只属于你的事，不再只属于你了。 它开始与截止日期、团队、客户、策略、金钱、声誉、势头挂钩…… 好奇心变成了路线图。 品味变成了决策。 玩耍变成了产出。 你曾经用来逃离世界的东西，变成了世界找到你的途径。 而现在又多了一层奇怪的感受： 机器也开始擅长这些工作了。 不只是那些无聊的部分。 而是那些曾经感觉贴近内心的部分。 写作、编程、设计、推理、做出有品味的决定、把模糊的想法变成真实的东西。 那些我们曾用来证明自己内心有某种特别之处的技能， 正在变成模型可以近似、重新组合，有时甚至做得更快的东西。 这以一种很具体的方式让人感到恐惧。 不仅仅是因为工作或竞争， 而是因为它触及了你围绕自己构建的那个神话。 如果我擅长的事，机器也能做， 那么其中真正属于我的部分是什么？ 我想，这个问题之所以痛苦，是因为它最终指向同一个地方。 最初的热爱。 在头衔之前，在公司之前，在品味变成角色之前， 在工作对别人有用之前， 内心曾有一团小小的火焰。 好奇心。痴迷。 那种当你对世界多理解一点，或者让一小片世界顺从你的意志时， 世界变得更加鲜活的感觉。 AI可以让产出更快。 它甚至可以提升技艺的下限。 但它无法替你渴望。 它无法决定什么值得去爱。 它无法守护那条让你最初在乎的、奇怪而私密的线索。 也许，这才是现在更重要的东西。 不是你能否仍然手工制作出那个作品。 不是你能否在每项任务上都胜过机器。 那场游戏已经在改变。 真正的问题是，你是否仍然与源头保持着联系。 那个没有观众的部分。 没有路线图。没有截止日期。 那个可以漫游、收集奇怪的参考、做无用之物的部分。 追随美，允许犯错，允许缓慢，做自己，保持真实。 因为那个部分并非与工作分离。 它是工作的源头。 如果你失去了它，你仍然可以运作。 你仍然可以管理机器。 你仍然可以提示、审查、决定、交付，让事情继续推进。 但作品会变得更单薄。更安全。更容易解释。更缺少生命力。 所以，也许真正的修行不是更努力地工作、更多地休息，或者少在乎一点。 也许是不断回到那个爱开始的地方—— 在它变得有用之前， 在它变得可读之前， 在任何人需要它提供什么之前， 甚至在机器能把它反射回给你之前。 不是为了逃离工作。 而是为了确保内心的火焰依然活着。
viewpoints.originalContent: when the dream becomes the job i used to think the dream was to make my hobby my work. to spend my life close to the things i loved: computers, tools, interfaces, systems, tiny details, the feeling of making something from nothing. the things i used to do at night, after school, after work, in the margins of life, somehow became the center of my life. and it is a dream. i don’t want to pretend otherwise. there is a very specific happiness in getting paid to care. in meeting other people who care. in building a language around your obsession. in seeing something that lived only in your head become real enough for other people to touch. but there is also a quiet pain in it. because the thing that once belonged only to you no longer belongs only to you. it becomes attached to deadlines, teams, customers, strategy, money, reputation, momentum... curiosity becomes roadmap. taste becomes decision-making. play becomes output. the thing you once used to escape the world becomes the thing through which the world reaches you. and now there is another strange layer: the machines are getting good at the work too. not just the boring parts. the parts that used to feel close to the heart. writing, coding, designing, reasoning, making taste-like decisions, turning vague ideas into something real. the things we once used as proof that we had something special inside us are becoming things a model can approximate, remix, and sometimes do faster. that can feel scary in a very specific way. not only because of jobs or competition, but because it touches the myth you built around yourself. if the thing i became good at can be done by a machine, then what part of it was really me? i think that question is painful because it arrives at the same place. the original love. before the title, before the company, before the taste became a role, before the work became useful to other people, there was a small fire inside. curiosity. obsession. the feeling that the world became more alive when you understood a little more of it, or made a tiny piece of it bend to your will. viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于AI领域未来可预见的结构性发展，几点思考如下： * 前沿智能持续突破，不断推动行业向前发展。顶尖实验室将继续采购最优质、最大量的数据，构建最强算力，引领训练技术突破等前沿方向。不同技术路线在定价和能力上形成市场分层，但整体竞争压力会降低单任务成本。不过随着时间推移，我们对模型的要求会越来越高——某项能力成本下降时，使用量就会激增——因此前沿领域的投入和需求仍将保持强劲。 * 开源权重快速吸收前沿突破（并在约束条件下催生其他突破方向），既提供更低成本的智能方案，又能针对特定工作流和领域进行后训练。这形成了对前沿领域的良性制衡——你可以随时在超大规模云服务商处以"成本价"运行模型，并针对自身任务微调模型。 * 应用层AI迎来重大机遇，可通过融合前沿智能与开源或低成本闭源模型，在任何领域编排工作流。凭借评估体系、深度领域认知、企业数据与工作流的可信度，该层能实现性能与成本的最优组合。应用层AI通常还会针对系统中高频、可预测的任务，部署自己的强化学习模型。 * 企业个体将普遍聚焦自身业务场景，确保任何AI系统都能持续优化地获取所需数据与信息。部分企业（如大型银行、制药公司等）会针对特定业务领域训练专属模型，在权衡利弊后获取真正的竞争优势，但多数企业会将精力投入在确保自身数据和工作流能充分吸收AI突破的成果上。 总而言之：尽管某些环节看似零和博弈，但技术栈各层及不同发展路径都蕴含着巨大机遇。
viewpoints.originalContent: A few thoughts on what we will see in AI structurally for the foreseeable future: * Frontier intelligence continues unabated and pushes the industry forward continuously. The top labs will continue to buy the best and the most data, build the most compute, be at the forefront of improved training breakthroughs, and so on. A few different approaches stratify the market on pricing and capability, but overall competitive pressure brings down pricing on a per task basis. That said, we just ask more from the models over time - as one thing gets cheaper, we just use more - so frontier spend and use remains robust. * Open weights rapidly absorbs frontier breakthroughs (and drives other breakthrough directions given the constraints), offering both lower cost intelligence and the ability to be post trained for specific workflows and domains. This creates a healthy counter balance to the frontier as you can run models “at cost” on a hyperscaler at any time, and tune models just for your tasks. * The Applied AI layer has a huge opportunity to combine frontier intelligence with open or cheap closed models to orchestrate workflows in any given domain. Due to evals, deep domain context, being trusted with enterprise data and workflows, this layer can maximize performance and cost combination. The applied AI layer will also often have their own RLed models especially for high volume, predictable tasks in their systems. * Individual enterprises will generally focus on their enterprise context, making sure they can get any AI system the right data and information to work with, in a continuously improving way. Some will go off and train their own models for specific areas of work (large banks, pharma, etc.) where they can get real alpha from doing so given the many tradeoffs, but most will spend energy on making sure they can get all of the gains from AI breakthroughs on their data and workflows. Net net: even though some of this gets framed as zero sum, there’s just a ton of opportunity for all layers of the stack and approaches.

viewpoints.translatedContent: Codex 与 ChatGPT Work 用户的更新。没有削弱，只有好消息！ - 我们已完成推理优化，并将节省的成本回馈给所有 GPT-5.6 Sol 订阅用户。仅此一项，使用量将增加约 10%。 - 我们发现，将 GPT-5.6 Sol 的上下文长度限制从 GPT-5.5 的 272k 提升至 372k 后，导致计费使用量超出预期。现已恢复至 272k，并将在未来几天内重新推出 372k。此更改后，您应会注意到使用量消耗显著减少。 - 为查明额外使用量的来源，我们进行了一些实验，调整了推理强度（内部称为“juice 值”），现已恢复原状。 - 在高和极高推理强度下，多智能体的使用量略高于预期，我们正在修复此问题。同时，还修复了自动审查中可提升效率的一个小问题。此外，5 小时限制暂时仍不适用。 祝周末愉快！
viewpoints.originalContent: Updates for Codex and ChatGPT Work users. No nerfing, only good stuff! - We have landed inference optimizations and are passing down savings to all the subscriptions for GPT-5.6 Sol. That should result in around 10% more usage on its own. - We noticed that by changing the context size limit in the product to 372k for GPT-5.6 Sol, up from 272k for GPT-5.5, it resulted in more usage being charged than intended. We have reverted to 272k and will work to roll back out to 372k in the days to come. You should notice that usage drains significantly less after this change. - To understand where the extra usage was coming from, we ran some experiments where reasoning efforts were changed (referred to as juice values under the hood) and have reverted this. - There is slightly more usage of multi-agent than intended in high and xhigh reasoning effort, we are fixing this going forward. Also fixing a small other thing we noticed with auto-review where we can be more efficient. And we continue to have the 5h limit temporarily not apply. Enjoy the rest of the weekend!
viewpoints.role: Codex & ChatGPT OpenAI

viewpoints.translatedContent: 21世纪商业领域的关键架构问题之一，将是如何在人工智能模型承载海量智能的时代，最大化企业知识产权——以决策、洞察、工作流模式和最佳实践的形式呈现。人们或许认为这些问题会因"苦涩教训"而自然消解，但现实恰恰相反：随着智能愈发强大，这些议题反而变得更为关键。当任何企业都能获取前沿智能时，如何独特地运用它便成为核心命题。这正是企业与底层人工智能之间仍存在巨大价值创造空间的原因。为工作流建立评估体系、确保能调度不同智能层级的模型、以改进自身工作流的方式捕获轨迹、并确保信息价值随人工智能进步而持续累积——这些都将成为至关重要的考量。这也解释了为何当前应用人工智能层存在如此巨大的机遇。那些能帮助其他企业破解这些难题的公司，将最有可能赢得下一代企业工作负载的竞争。
viewpoints.originalContent: One of the key architectural questions of the 21st century in business will be how you maximize your corporate IP in the form of decisions, insights, workflow patterns, and best practices in a world where so much intelligence is packed into AI models. One might think these questions could just get bitter lessoned out of existence, but in reality they become even more germane as intelligence becomes more powerful. In a world where any firm also has access to frontier intelligence, understanding how you leverage it uniquely becomes a critical question. That’s why so much value is left to be created between the enterprise and the underlying AI itself. Having evals for your workflows, ensuring that you can route models from different tiers of intelligence, capturing traces in a way that improve your own workflows, and making sure the value of your information compounds as AI gets better all become critical considerations. Which is also why there’s so much opportunity right now in the applied AI layer. The companies that help figure this out for other enterprises will be in the best position to win the next enterprise workloads.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 人工智能本应取代的工作，却出现了与预期相反的结果。软件行业的职位发布数量正超过其他领域。这是为什么呢？如果降低某种用途广泛产品的生产成本，人们就会想要生产更多。我们在工业领域不断见证这一现象，如今终于在知识工作中看到了同样的趋势。由于软件的单位成本大幅降低，人们对其需求激增。于是，我们开始将软件应用于各种新事物，个人和企业启动的软件项目比以往任何时候都多。但由于这项工作本身并未完全自动化（而且在可预见的未来很可能也不会），你仍然需要懂这些系统的人来维护代码、决定构建方向、长期运行、更新等等。这一切都需要人力投入。随着我们降低以往极为稀缺工作领域的生产成本，同样的现象也将在许多其他领域发生。智能体带来的将是更丰富的产出，而非简单的替代。
viewpoints.originalContent: The job that AI was supposed to replace is experiencing the opposite of the expected outcome. Software job postings are outpacing other fields. Why is that? If you lower the cost of production of something that has lots of use cases, people want more things produced. We’ve seen this play out in the industrial world constantly, and now we’re finally seeing it in knowledge work. Because software now is much lower to cost per unit, people want way more of it. So we start to use software for all new things and people and companies light up more software projects than ever before. But because the job itself is not fully automated (and likely won’t be for as far out as we can see), you still need people that understand these systems to maintain the code, decide what to build, run it over the long run, update it, and more. That all requires people to do work. The same thing is going to happen in many other fields as well as we bring down the cost of production of previously extremely scarce areas of work. Agents will cause more abundance than replacement.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 如果你在思考企业级应用人工智能，这是一篇很棒的帖子。这篇帖子的标题是关于哪些公司能从人工智能中获得巨大收益，但最深刻的内容在于人工智能转型在组织中的实际样貌。其核心在于改变底层的工作流程或业务流程。随着我们从聊天工具转向智能代理，这些代理实际上必须针对工作流程进行部署，而这些流程通常跨越组织中的多个职能。这与仅仅将人工智能推广给最终用户的方式截然不同。前期需要投入更多工作，但成果才是真正能带来显著投资回报率的东西。“软件要求员工去适应一个工具，而基础设施则改变了员工脚下的操作层。员工仍应了解发生了什么，流程负责人仍应能够暂停工作流、更改规则、批准例外情况，或在需要时将人员重新拉回流程中。但价值不应依赖于某人每天记得使用人工智能。”这场竞赛的赢家将是那些能够针对特定工作流程和业务流程进行部署，并具备深厚领域专业知识的平台。这套策略通常需要大量的前端支持、变革管理、数据的有序组织、能够对工作流程进行全面评估，以及许多其他要素才能做好。
viewpoints.originalContent: This is a great post if youre thinking about applied AI in the enterprise. The headline of this post is about what companies have huge upside from AI, but the deepest nuggets are about what AI transformation looks like in an organization. It’s fundamentally about changing the underlying workflow or business process. As we move from chat tools to agents, those agents actually have to be deployed against workflows, which usually span multiple functions in an org. This is a different way of deploying AI than solely rolling it out to end users. It takes much more work upfront, but the results are the things that actually drive significant ROI. “Software asks the employee to adopt a tool, but infrastructure changes the operating layer underneath the employee. The employee should still know what happened, and the process owner should still be able to pause the workflow, change a rule, approve an exception, or pull a person back in when needed. But the value should not depend on someone remembering to use the AI every day.” The winners of this will be the platforms that can be deployed for specific workflows and business processes with a deep domain expertise. The playbook will often heavily require FDE support, change management, getting data well organized, be able to have comprehensive evals for the workflows, and much more to get right.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于未来竞争优势的思考，这篇帖子精彩地剖析了当AI模型在企业间共享、并承载着行业大量智慧时，需要深入考量的动态因素。这将成为未来十年乃至更久，企业乃至整个经济面临的核心问题。如果AI在每个行业——如法律、金融、医疗或生命科学——都基于最优质的数据集进行训练，那么未来你该如何竞争并实现差异化？这是一个绝佳的开放性问题，鉴于AI进展之快，我认为目前还无法完全预知答案。但归根结底，道理显而易见：如果智慧变得充裕且对领域内任何人都触手可及，那么那些能最有效地运用它，并依托一套随时间增值的数据与知识体系的企业，将占据强势地位。在模型所蕴含的智慧、企业自有数据、这些数据与AI在其工作流中的连接，以及员工最终如何与这一系统互动以创造价值之间，存在着一个巨大的强化循环。在一个垂直领域内，所有企业达到统一状态并无明显节点，因为每家企业都会以不同方式应对，正如它们目前在人才和工作流上的做法一样。甚至可以说，那些做得最好的企业将获得复利效应，使其优势随时间加速扩大。总体而言，观察这一问题将如何随时间演变，极其引人入胜。
viewpoints.originalContent: Great post on some of the dynamics to think through for the future competitive advantage in world when AI models are shared amongst firms and packing so much for the intelligence of that industry. This is going to become a core question for companies and the economy broadly over the next decade and beyond. If AI is trained on the best datasets in every single industry - like law, finance, healthcare, or life sciences - then how do you compete and differentiate in the future? This is a great open question that I don’t think is perfectly knowable right now because of how fast AI progress is happening. But ultimately it stands to reason that if intelligence is abundant and broadly available to anyone in a field, then the companies that effectively use it the best and against a set of data and knowledge that grows in value over time, will be in a strong position. There’s a huge reinforcing loop between the intelligence from models, a company’s own data, the connection of that data and AI in their workflows, and how employees ultimately interact with that system to create value. There’s no obvious point where this will become uniform across all companies in a vertical because each company will approach this in a different way, just as they already do with their talent and workflows. If anything, there will be compounding returns to those that do this best that accelerate their advantage over time. Overall, super interesting question to see how this plays out over time.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 刚结束与几十位企业IT负责人的会议，围绕AI智能体展开讨论。以下是几个突出的共同主题： * 大量讨论聚焦于必须解决运营模式挑战，才能充分释放AI价值。多数公司的组织架构长期处于孤岛状态，而智能体在贯穿这些孤岛的流程中才能发挥最大效能。因此核心问题在于：如何开始部署能跨组织边界运作的集中管理型智能体？由谁管理？如何部署并推动落地？ * 数据碎片化仍是多数组织的重大难题。只要数据高度分散且格式不统一，或无法触达合适的人员与智能体，企业就会面临智能体输出结果不准确或不符合业务规范的问题。这既涉及结构化数据（产品指标或营收数据），也涉及非结构化数据（产品路线图或客户合同）。 * 企业普遍意识到需要明确未来的核心数据护城河。若所有人都能通过各类模型获取大致相同的超级智能，那么未来为模型提供的上下文将成为专有价值。捕获这些数据并将其转化为智能体可用的格式变得至关重要。 * 所有人都在摸索衡量AI应用成效的正确指标。普遍共识是令牌本身并非理想指标，人们更倾向于业务成果（理想状态下）。但针对业务成果（如增收或增产），必须深入每个具体工作流才能判断AI是否成功实现转型，因此自上而下的管理难度更大。 * 越来越多观点认为企业将生活在多模型并存的世界。人们对能基于成本或性能将工作负载路由至不同模型（前端或开放权重）的中间层兴趣浓厚（尽管实际应用尚处早期）。同时企业也在探索哪些任务直接交给模型处理，哪些应剥离为横向系统与上下文，以便随时替换任意系统。 * 推动AI应用与落地的人才仍是重大议题和挑战。许多人认为由于外部相关人才短缺，必须通过内部培训解决。顺带一提，这对擅长企业级智能体部署与管理的人而言仍是巨大机遇，因为多数公司都在寻觅这类技能。 * AI的最佳应用场景往往是彻底改变工作方式，而非简单替代现有流程并提升效率。各企业正根据行业特性探索自身路径，这通常既是AI最令人振奋的应用，也是最具高回报潜力的方向。 近期还探讨了更多议题，但总体而言，变革浪潮汹涌，未来仍有无限可能。
viewpoints.originalContent: Just coming off of meetings with a couple dozen enterprise IT leaders discussing AI agents. Here are a few of the common themes that stand out: * Lots of conversation that you have to solve an operating model challenge to get the full benefits of AI. Most companies have orgs that have always operated in siloes; but agents are most effectively when they are tied to a process, which often cuts across these siloes. So the big question is how do you start to deploy centrally managed agents that can work across organizational boundaries. Who manages these agents? How do they get deployed and adopted? * Data fragmentation remains a major issue for most organizations. As long as data remains highly fragmented and not in standard formats, or data is not available to the right people and agents, enterprises are dealing with issues around being able to get answers from agents that are accurate or that conform to their business practices. This cuts across both systems with structured data (product metrics or revenue figures) and unstructured data (product roadmap or customer contracts). * Clear sense that companies need to figure out what their core data moats are going to be in the future. If everyone has access to roughly the same superintelligence from the various models, then the context that you feed the models becomes proprietary value in the future. Capturing this data and getting it into a format that agents can use becomes very important. * Everyone is trying to figure out the right metrics to manage to for AI adoption. General consensus that tokens are not the right metric per se, and people leaning more toward business outcomes (in an ideal world). For business outcomes (like more revenue or more shipped product), though, you have to get close to each individual workflow to figure out if it was successfully transformed with AI so it’s harder to manage top down. * Growing view that enterprises are going to live in a multi-model world. Lots of interest (though early in actual adoption) in layers that can route workloads to different models (frontside or open weights) for cost or performance reasons. Also enterprises are trying to figure out what things do you give…

viewpoints.translatedContent: 公开网络上可供所有模型训练或代理操作的有用数据只占很小一部分。大部分数据存在于组织内部，往往分散在遗留系统、员工头脑中，或是零散地分布在整个企业里。这些数据包括每家公司的营销计划、产品路线图、开发实践、合同、财务数据、战略以及通用企业知识。无论是用于模型训练，还是作为代理的上下文，这些数据随着时间的推移将变得越来越有价值。能否安全地将正确数据提供给代理进行操作，将成为未来公司运营和竞争的一个决定性特征。在经济活动中，人工智能的有效运用，很大程度上将取决于哪些公司能让代理最深入地理解其业务，并代表公司做出正确决策。数据确实是新的石油。
viewpoints.originalContent: A small percentage of useful data is on the open web available to all models for training or for agents to operate with. Most of it lives inside of organizations and often is in legacy systems, in people’s heads, or is fragmented across the enterprise. It’s the marketing plans, product roadmaps, development practices, contracts, financial data, strategies, and general corporate knowledge that every company operates off of. Whether it’s for training a model or used as context for agents, this data will increasingly be more valuable over time. The ability to get the right data to agents to operate on, securely, will be a defining characteristic of how companies operate and compete in the future. Effective use of AI will in the economy will largely come down to the companies that are able to have agents best understand their business and make the right decisions on their behalf. Data actually is the new oil.
viewpoints.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于如何思考开源AI与应用AI层的精彩文章。前沿智能与定制模型这两件事在AI领域将始终成立。前沿智能可能持续引领全新用例的解决，并常用于编排规划各类复杂工作流。与此同时，当企业场景中的用例趋于成熟可预测时，您就可以开始剥离部分令牌，转而采用成本更低的开源或闭源模型，或是针对特定任务训练的模型。在任何新用例的采用曲线上过早实施这一策略都毫无意义，因为您尚不清楚优化目标，这也解释了为何此处总会存在些许滞后。这个过程本质上可以永续运行，因为前沿智能与调优模型的优势都没有终点。正因如此，两种方案的开支与令牌消耗量在未来数年仍将持续攀升——我们在两方面都仍处于早期阶段。需要重申的是，这种动态之所以可能实现，完全得益于应用AI层能够有效评估特定领域的工作流、选择混合模型来完成任务，并具备足够规模最终训练出专属模型。
viewpoints.originalContent: Great post on how to think about open source AI and the applied AI layer. Two things will always be true in AI. Frontier intelligence will likely remain at the forefront of solving brand new used cases and often be used for orchestrating and planning of any type of complex workflow. At the same time, as use-cases become mature and predictable in an enterprise context, you can begin to peel off some set of the tokens to either lower cost open or closed models *or* models that are trained for the task at hand. Doing this too early in the adoption curve of any new use-case doesn’t make sense as you don’t know what you’re optimizing for, which is why there will always be a bit of a lag here. This process can essentially run on forever as there is no end for both the benefits of frontier intelligence or tuned models. This is why the spend and token volume for both approaches will continue to go up for years to come as we’re still early on both. Again, the only reason this dynamic is possible though is because of the applied AI layer that can effectively eval their workflows in a specific domain, choose a mixture of models to solve tasks, and have enough scale to eventually train their own models for their purposes.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 人工智能领域的竞争，正逐渐演变为一场对上下文的争夺。AI的一切都围绕着如何让智能体尽可能高效运转。这种高效性，取决于智能体是否具备正确的领域专业知识，能否获取恰当的上下文和工具，以及它们融入工作流程的方式是否能让用户轻松交互、审核其成果，并将其整合到后续流程中。因此，那些能在智能体中捕获并利用最优质、最丰富上下文的平台——并且能为任务选择最合适模型的平台——将成为智能体发挥最佳效能的舞台。只需看看编程智能体、法律智能体或客服智能体，就能明白这种规模化应用的模样。这正是应用层AI的价值远不止于大语言模型包装壳的原因。能够为手头工作组织关键知识，并以受管控的方式维护这些知识，确保只有合适的人员和智能体才能访问，同时随着时间推移不断优化智能体的上下文，这种能力至关重要。久而久之，这一层将能在多种模型间调度工作，利用前沿智能进行规划、编排和审核，并在大量任务间隙使用成本更低的模型组合（无论是开源还是闭源）。应用层也处于有利位置，能够训练和开发专为其领域量身定制的自有模型。虽然永远不应低估“苦涩的教训”，但在许多情况下，采用接近前沿的基础模型，并针对单一领域工作进行后训练，往往能降低成本或提升特定任务的表现。最后，应用层也是工作流程中大部分变革管理需要发生的地方。这就是为什么全栈领域专家在应用层如此重要，因为正是在这个节点，客户需要由特定供应商解决具体的业务问题。任何能以端到端方式彻底解决这些问题的公司，都将构筑起最深的护城河。日复一日，我们正逐渐看清AI领域可能呈现的长期市场格局。
viewpoints.originalContent: The battle in AI is shaping up to be a battle for context. Everything in AI is about making sure that agents are effective as possible. That effectiveness comes down to whether the agent has the right domain expertise, access to the right context and tools to work with, and are involved in workflow in a way that users can easily interact with, review its work, and incorporate it into the rest of the process. As a consequence, the platforms that are able to capture and leverage the best and most context within their agents —and be able to pick the right models for the task- will be the place where agents do their best work. You can just look at coding agents, legal agents, or support agents as examples of what this looks like at scale. This is why the applied AI layer has a lot more value than just being an LLM wrapper. The ability to organize the critical knowledge for the work being done, and maintain this knowledge in a governed way where only the right people and agents have access, and the ability to improve the context for agents more and more over time, is critical. Over time, this layer will be able to route work between a variety of models, leveraging frontier intelligence for planning and orchestration and review, and a mix of lower cost models (open or closed) for the large volume of work between these tasks. The applied layer is also in a good position to train and develop its own models as well that are purpose built for their domains. Never good to bet against the bitter lesson, but equally taking a near frontier base model and post training it for just one type of domain work can -in many cases- lower costs or deliver better performance for certain tasks. Finally, this applied layer is also where most of the change management of the workflow will need to occur. This is why FDEs are so important at the applied layer, because this is the point where the customer needs to have specific business problem solved by a particular vendor. Whichever companies can solve that completely in an end-to-end fashion will have the greatest moats. As each day goes on, we’re learning more about what the likely long term market dynamics will look like in AI.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 在企业中部署人工智能，远不止与聊天机器人互动那么简单，这无疑需要付出切实努力，使AI系统与所涉及的基础业务流程对齐，并推动实现预期成果。大多数工作流程并非为AI代理直接嵌入而设计。如今企业中的工作流程面临数据碎片化、代理无法连接的遗留软件系统、依赖机构知识而非文档化知识等诸多问题。要大规模可靠部署代理，就需要清理数据、现代化IT系统、制定评估方案、推动新终端状态流程的变革管理等等。这还包括设计人类在流程中保留的环节（这将意味着人们与工作流程交互的全新方式），以及明确公司新的知识产权形态。正因如此，众多应用型AI公司正在扩大实地工程部署工作并推出部署公司，而实地工程部署角色将成为未来科技领域最关键的职位之一。在这方面，还有大量工作有待完成。
viewpoints.originalContent: The deployment of AI in the enterprise beyond just interacting with a chatbot will unequivocally take real work to align AI systems to the underlying business processes they’re involved in and drive the desired outcomes. Most workflows weren’t designed for AI agents to just drop into. Workflows today in the enterprise deal with fragmented data, legacy software systems that agents can’t connect with, institutional instead of documented knowledge, and more. To deploy agents reliably at scale you need to get data cleaned up, modernize IT systems, figure out evals, drive change management for the new end state process, and so on. This also involves designing where humans remain in the loop (which will mean entirely new ways people interact with the workflows), and figuring out what a company’s new IP looks like. This is why so many applied AI companies are expanding FDE efforts and launching deploycos, and why the FDE role will be one of the most critical jobs in tech going forward. There’s a tremendous amount of work to be done on this front.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我们一直将AI网关比作一个~~内容~~令牌分发网络，就像AI模型的CDN。CDN的一大亮点在于无需重新部署即可动态重路由或拦截流量。当Fable突然退役时，我们担心依赖它的生产工作负载会受影响。即便抛开Fable不谈，由于GPU资源竞争激烈，模型退役其实相当常见。但我们的数据显示，仍有用户在使用旧版模型进行愉快的生产流量！现在，我们通过AI网关规则来解决这个问题。例如：您现在可以即时重写模型"路由"！ 𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚊𝚒-𝚐𝚊𝚝𝚎𝚠𝚊𝚢 𝚛𝚞𝚕𝚎𝚜 𝚊𝚍𝚍 \ --𝚝𝚢𝚙𝚎 𝚛𝚎𝚠𝚛𝚒𝚝𝚎 \ --𝚜𝚘𝚞𝚛𝚌𝚎 𝚊𝚗𝚝𝚑𝚛𝚘𝚙𝚒𝚌/𝚌𝚕𝚊𝚞𝚍𝚎-𝚏𝚊𝚋𝚕𝚎-𝟻 \ --𝚍𝚎𝚜𝚝𝚒𝚗𝚊𝚝𝚒𝚘𝚗 𝚊𝚗𝚝𝚑𝚛𝚘𝚙𝚒𝚌/𝚌𝚕𝚊𝚞𝚍𝚎-𝚘𝚙𝚞𝚜-𝟻 这进一步丰富了AI网关挽回丢失令牌的手段和技术储备。令牌一旦丢失，您就会损失收入和客户💸 感谢@rtaneja_ @crowprose @shaper——我们从CLI设计到生产级能力落地，速度非常快！
viewpoints.originalContent: We've been explaining AI Gateway as a C̶o̶n̶t̶e̶n̶t̶ Token Delivery Network. Like a CDN for AI models. One great feature of CDNs is the ability to dynamically re-route or deny traffic without redeployment. When Fable was suddenly retired, we worried about production workloads depending on it. Even Fable aside, models get retired quite often as GPU capacity is heavily contested. Yet our data shows people still having happy production traffic of older model versions! We're solving this now with AI Gateway Rules. e.g.: you can now rewrite model "routes" on the fly! 𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚊𝚒-𝚐𝚊𝚝𝚎𝚠𝚊𝚢 𝚛𝚞𝚕𝚎𝚜 𝚊𝚍𝚍 \ --𝚝𝚢𝚙𝚎 𝚛𝚎𝚠𝚛𝚒𝚝𝚎 \ --𝚜𝚘𝚞𝚛𝚌𝚎 𝚊𝚗𝚝𝚑𝚛𝚘𝚙𝚒𝚌/𝚌𝚕𝚊𝚞𝚍𝚎-𝚏𝚊𝚋𝚕𝚎-𝟻 \ --𝚍𝚎𝚜𝚝𝚒𝚗𝚊𝚝𝚒𝚘𝚗 𝚊𝚗𝚝𝚑𝚛𝚘𝚙𝚒𝚌/𝚌𝚕𝚊𝚞𝚍𝚎-𝚘𝚙𝚞𝚜-𝟻 This adds to the repertoire of capabilities and techniques AI Gateway brings to the table to recover lost tokens. If you drop tokens, you lose revenue and customers 💸 Kudos to @rtaneja_ @crowprose @shaper – we went from CLI design to production-grade capability very quickly!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 更多数据表明，AI应用与就业的关系与许多人的预期恰恰相反。Ramp发现，企业AI应用程度越高，员工人数增长越快。在Box，我们最近对1600多家中大型企业进行了调查，结果与此类似。58%的受访者预计未来三年员工人数将增加。有趣的是，在AI应用最成熟的企业中，这一比例攀升至79%。AI应用越深入的企业，未来员工人数的预期增长率也越高。当然，能够大力投入AI的企业，往往也是业务增长较快的企业，这自然会带动员工人数增加。所以，这个故事的重点并不在于应用AI就一定会带来增长。*但*最重要的启示是，相反的情况并未出现。几年前人们担心，AI应用最多的企业会减少招聘。但实际上，这才是你应该预料到的结果。如果一家企业利用AI进行销售，获取客户或市场情报，从而赢得更多客户，他们就会招聘更多而非更少的销售人员。如果你能开发出比以前多得多的软件，最终你会雇佣更多工程师，因为项目规模会扩大，承接的任务也会增多。其他领域也是如此。
viewpoints.originalContent: More data is showing the opposite of what many people expected with AI adoption and jobs. Ramp found that the more AI adoption a company has the more their headcount grows. At Box, we recently did a survey of 1,600+ mid and large sized companies, and the findings were similar. 58% of respondents expected headcount to rise over the next three years. Interestingly, that figure climbs to 79% among the most mature adopters of AI. The more advanced AI adopters expected to grow their headcount at a greater rate in the future than others. Of course it's true that the companies that can afford to adopt AI the most are also the ones that likely are seeing growth in their business, leading to more headcount. So the point of the story isn't necessarily that by adopting AI you will inherently grow. *But* the most important takeaway is that the opposite is not proving out. The fears a couple years ago would have been that the companies adopting AI the most would be hiring fewer people. But in reality this is what actually you should expect to happen. If a company can get more customers because they use AI in sales for account or market intelligence, they hire more sales people not fewer. If you can build way more software than before, you end up hiring more engineers because the projects get bigger and you take on more. And so on.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 《神鬼寓言》的情况似乎在好转，接下来大概就是GPT-5.6了。我们目前所看到的，是前沿模型发布（或至少是那些具备显著编程和网络能力的模型）未来可能呈现的初步先例。这大概也适用于人工智能安全组织所识别的生物及其他风险类别。引用Anthropic的博文：“3. 共享的行业框架。尽管我们达成了建设性的解决方案，但这些事件清楚地表明，行业需要一种一致的方式来评估和修复人工智能模型潜在的‘越狱’问题（即绕过模型安全防护的技术）。2 一个用于判断特定越狱严重程度的共享标准，将有助于人工智能开发者在发现新问题时进行分类，更安全地推出高能力模型，并向政府和行业合作伙伴一致地传达风险级别。我们已与亚马逊、微软、谷歌及其他Glasswing合作伙伴着手开发这样一个框架，并在下文概述。4. 更深入的政府合作。我们也在加强与美国政府在新型发布前测试、信息共享和研究合作方面的协作。我们在最后一节描述了这种更深入的合作。”走到这一步的过程颇为混乱，但至少有了一个看似可行的框架雏形。这里唯一需要警惕的是，各种风险及其在实际中可被利用的程度，存在很大的主观性。对于重大发布，我们很可能将依赖一个需要大量判断以及实验室与政府之间反复沟通的框架。我们所能期望的最好结果，是这个过程相对高效，并有望在模型的增量版本更新时得以加速。如果在此能力阈值之后，每次发布都需要经历同样的审查流程，导致我们无法保持迄今所见的突破速度，那将是一个糟糕的结果。
viewpoints.originalContent: Things seem to be ending up in a better spot with Fable, and presumably GPT-5.6 next. What we have now is the initial precedent for what frontier model releases (or at least those that have significant coding and cyber capabilities) could look like going forward. This would presumably apply to bio and other categories of risk that have been identified by AI safety groups. From the Anthropic post: “3. A shared industry framework. Although we have reached a constructive resolution, these events have made clear that the industry needs a consistent way to assess and fix potential “jailbreaks” of AI models (techniques that bypass a model’s safeguards).2 A shared standard for judging the severity of a given jailbreak would help AI developers triage new findings as they arise, launch highly-capable models with greater safety, and communicate the level of risk consistently to government and industry partners. Together with Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and other Glasswing partners, we’ve started to develop such a framework, and we outline it below. 4. Deeper government collaboration. We’re also strengthening our level of collaboration with the US government on new pre-release testing, information sharing, and research collaboration. We describe this deeper collaboration in the final section.” It’s been a messy process to get here, but at least there’s some semblance of a framework that could be practical. The only note of caution here would be that there’s a lot of subjectivity that goes into various risks and their actual levels of exploitability in practice. We’re likely going to be living with a framework that requires heavy judgment and back and forth between labs and the government for major releases. The best we can hope for is that this is a relatively efficient process, and hopefully has ways of being sped up for incremental version updates in models. It would be a bad outcome if every release after this level of threshold of capability required the same review process, and we don’t get the same rate of breakthroughs we’ve been seeing.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我们一直在通过Box AI复杂工作评估（Box AI Complex Work Eval）测试Anthropic的Claude Sonnet 5，这是我们的智能体基准测试，让模型端到端地处理真实的企业文档工作。Sonnet 5在复杂的多步骤工作中保持了前沿级质量，并在能源（+4.7个百分点）、零售（+4.4个百分点）和专业服务（+2.6个百分点）等几个核心企业领域，以及其他非结构化数据极为复杂的场景中，领先于Sonnet 4.6。以下是与Sonnet 4.6相比的一些胜出示例，以便了解Sonnet 5中一些更高级的推理能力： * 融资尽职调查：它从原始资产负债表中计算了公司的流动性和杠杆比率，并发现源报告自身所述的债务股本比低估了杠杆水平，标记出所有三项贷款契约均被违反，而不仅仅是文件承认的那些。 * 大修成本分析：它根据公司自身的KPI定义界定了“总成本”，正确地将停产损失成本分离出来，因为指南要求单独跟踪，而不是简单地将表格上的每个数字相加。它还发现并处理了电子表格中的一个损坏引用单元格。 * SKU收入分析：在细分销售数据上，它针对正确的子类别分母计算了每个产品的贡献，避开了除以类别总额的常见错误，并标记了为何没有宠物类别的SKU进入前9名。 Sonnet 5将很快在Box AI Studio中提供，供客户构建自定义智能体。
viewpoints.originalContent: We've been running Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5 through the Box AI Complex Work Eval, our agentic benchmark that puts models through real enterprise document work end-to-end. Sonnet 5 holds frontier-class quality on complex multi-step work and pulls ahead of Sonnet 4.6 in several core enterprise domains like Energy (+4.7pp), Retail (+4.4pp), and Professional Services (+2.6pp), and other spaces where unstructured data is heavily complex. Here are a few examples of wins compared to Sonnet 4.6 to get a sense of some of the more advanced reasoning capabilities in Sonnet 5: * Financing due diligence: It computed the company's liquidity and leverage ratios from the raw balance sheet, and caught that the source report's own stated debt-to-equity figure understated the leverage, flagging all three loan covenants as violated, not just the ones the document admitted. * Overhaul cost analysis: It scoped "total cost" to the company's own KPI definitions, correctly separating out Lost Production Cost because the guidance said to track it separately rather than naively summing every number on the sheet. It also caught and handled a broken reference cell in the spreadsheet. * SKU revenue analysis: On segmented sales data, it computed each product's contribution against the correct subcategory denominator, sidestepping the easy mistake of dividing by the category total, and flagged why no Pet-category SKU cracked the top 9. Sonnet 5 will be available in the Box AI Studio shortly for customers to build custom agents with.

viewpoints.title: 传统产品经理在适应AI原生开发时面临的最大挑战，是缺乏天马行空的想象力。十年来对框架、"敏捷"和指标的痴迷，导致了以约束为先、渐进式的思维模式。我过去常在团队中对抗这种倾向，方法是让大家想象我们拥有100年后的未来科技，设想它能实现怎样的体验，再反向推导——这样产生的创意总是更具突破性。有趣的是，那种未来科技其实已经到来。去创造那些不可思议的事物吧！

viewpoints.originalContent: The biggest challenge for trad PMs trying to adapt to AI native building is a lack of magical thinking. A decade of frameworks, “agile” and metric obsession has led to constraint-first, incremental thinking. I used to combat this on my teams by asking them to imagine we had tech from 100 yrs in the future, the experiences it would enable and working backward from that. the ideas would always be far more creative. the funny thing is, that technology from the future is here. go build that magical thing!

viewpoints.originalContent: Some good best practices here on AI token cost optimization. None of these happens though without a deep understanding of the underlying work being done in a non-abstract way. The ultimate implication is that a layer between the work itself and the underlying intelligence needs to deeply understand your workflows, context, and business process. Now, each individual company doing this on their own is unlikely to be effective at scale, so as a consequence, this is effectively the playbook for any applied AI company right now. By evaling the models for the applied use cases, deeply understanding the domain, having tuned UX and features for the use case, and having the ability to support adoption and change (via FDEs), allow this layer to add a ton of value. And as a result, enterprises get higher ROI because you actually can get *more* intelligence per dollar by having optimal architecture and workflows. There will be many horizontal and vertical versions of this approach. Huge opportunity right now.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 尘埃落定后，关于品味的评论让我觉得真正好笑的是，这些评论来自很多从未真正建造过任何东西的人……不置身其中，你根本无法获得（或打磨）品味。这就像一位厨师做饭，指望第一道菜就能一次成功。但当你反复尝试100次，或许做了100道菜之后，第101道菜就会融入那10,000次迭代中的所有经验教训。然而，如果你过度拟合而缺乏变化，人们就会厌倦，因为他们也想要一些新东西。最优秀的人能够通过不断打破模式来学习、融入并创新。看看人工智能如何做到同样的事会很有趣——与大多数人不同，我认为它确实有相当的机会真正培养出品味。牢骚完毕。
viewpoints.originalContent: Now that the dust is settled, what’s really funny to me about the taste commentary is it’s coming from a LOT of people who never have built anything.. You can’t achieve (or refine) taste without being in the arena. It’s like a chef cooking and expecting their first dish to be good on the first go. But, when you give it a 100 iterations and maybe cook a 100 dishes, then the 101st one has imbued all the lessons from those 10,000 iterations. But, if you over fit without much variation, then people get tired of it since well they want something new as well. The best people are able to learn, imbue and innovate by breaking patterns consistently. It’ll be interesting to see how AI does the same - and unlike most people I think it has a fair shot at actually building taste. End rant.

They involve multiple steps of computation across functions and sandboxes, touching dozens of API services that can go down, rate limit you, etc. Nailing down observability out of the box for https://t.co/nDDXqUmOlD on Vercel was a key priority for the team, and the feedback so far has been 🔥↓

viewpoints.translatedContent: 重磅消息：OpenAI 发布了 GPT-5.6 Sol！即日起，根据美国政府指令，该模型仅限约 20 家预先批准的公司使用，而 @every 并不在名单之列。这似乎是临时性安排，政府正加紧制定针对具备先进能力的前沿模型的长期发布政策。我理解并赞同政府需要实施一定监管，以增强美国基础设施抵御网络攻击及防范此类模型被滥用所带来的其他潜在新威胁。但我同样坚信，让前沿模型实现广泛的民主化使用，对于我国在人工智能竞赛中保持领先地位绝对至关重要。这也关系到美国劳动者能否及时掌握新时代所需的新技能，从而保持高效生产力。若先进模型仅被锁在 AI 巨头和少数几家公司的员工手中，那么胸怀大志的学生、独立开发者以及职场专业人士，都将失去学习、创造和充分施展才华所必需的工具。此外，我谨代表 @every 以及与我们共享早期访问权限的开发者与创作者社群发声：我们的职责是尽早测试这些工具，以便帮助美国民众做好充分准备，学会如何最大限度地运用它们。若失去访问权限，我们便无法出色完成这项重要使命。所幸的是，OpenAI 与政府似乎都在努力推动尽快实现广泛开放。届时，我们定会第一时间进行体验评测 :)
viewpoints.originalContent: BREAKING: OpenAI announced GPT-5.6 Sol! As of today, by U.S. government directive, access is limited to only ~20 pre-approved companies and @every is not on the list. This appears to be a temporary situation while the government races to figure out a long-term policy for releasing frontier models with advanced capabilities. I understand and applaud the need for some government oversight in making American infrastructure resilient to cyberattacks and other potential new threats from the misuse of these models. However, I also strongly believe that widespread democratic access to frontier models is absolutely necessary to our country’s leading position in the AI race. It’s also critical for allowing American workers to keep pace with the new skills they need to be productive in this era. A world where advanced models are locked up only for use by the employees of AI giants and a select few companies is one where ambitious students, independent builders, and working professionals are denied the tools they need to learn, create, and compete to their fullest potential. Also, speaking for @every and the community of developers and writers who share early access with us: Our job is to test these tools early so that we can prepare Americans for how to use them to their fullest extent. If we lose access, we lose the ability to do that important job well. Thankfully, both OpenAI and the government seem to be working to make broad access available soon. We’ll be ready to vibe check when that happens :)

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我们如今已有了事实上的AI监管。从今往后，具备特定能力水平或基于特定算力规模训练的模型，在发布前很可能需要接受政府审查，这背后的原因并不难理解。现实来看，随着AI模型日益强大，这种局面本就难以避免（我认为为时过早，但事已至此）。所以现在，思考由此产生的各种影响和情景，反倒成了最值得玩味的事。其中几点包括： * 美国得以掌控谁能获取前沿智能、以及何时获取。只要我们能始终站在前沿、没有被他国赶超的风险，这套机制大体就能奏效。目前我们在前沿智能领域优势明显，因此这算是个稳妥的赌注，但许多雄心勃勃的势力正渴望改变这一格局。 * 这很可能导致AI发布出现积压，意味着模型进展中那种快速交替的跳跃式迭代会减少。乐观/理想的情况是，每次发布带来的能力跃升幅度更大，只是节奏放缓，最终我们仍能抵达原本会达到的同一节点。悲观的情况则是，那些渐进式的小幅跃迁，对于维持创新的持续飞轮本是必不可少的。 * 其他国家很可能更有动力至少通过主权AI战略来对冲风险，以免在所有时刻都依赖美国的AI供应。此前这基本无关紧要，因为替代方案不够好，但出于现实需要，以及我们在中国看到的情况，这种局面可能改变。 * 开放权重模型显然是这里的大赢家，它很可能成为主权AI构建的基础，并且（就目前而言）仍能在不受同等管控的情况下向市场发布。一个有趣的问题是，监管最终将如何延伸到开放模型，而这会带来一系列长期后果。 总之，鉴于我们如今在AI身上看到的能力，每个人对AI监管的思维模型都迎来了重大更新。真是疯狂的时代。
viewpoints.originalContent: We now have de facto AI regulation. It’s not obvious why from here on out models that have certain levels of capability or are trained on certain compute sizes won’t have to be reviewed by the government before release. Realistically, as AI models became more and more powerful this was going to be inevitable (I think it’s too early, but here we are). So now it’s mostly just interesting to think about the implications and scenarios from here. A few would be: * America gets to control who gets access to frontier intelligence and when. This generally works as long as we remain at the frontier at all times and don’t have a risk of being surpassed. At the moment we have a clear lead in frontier intelligence so this is a good bet, but lots of motivated parties would love to change that. * This likely creates backlog of AI releases which means that we will see less rapid fire back and forth jumps in model progress. Bull/fine case is that we just get bigger step functions per release at a slower rate and we end up at the same point we would have. Bear case is those incremental smaller jumps were necessary for the continued flywheel of innovation. * Other countries likely have even more incentive to at least hedge their bets with sovereign AI strategies so aren’t dependent on access to US AI all times. Previously this was relatively moot because the alternative wasn’t good enough, but that could change out of necessity and what we’re seeing in China. * Open weights obviously a big winner here as it becomes what likely sovereign AI gets built out on, and what (for now) can still be released to the market without the same controls. One interesting question would be how regulation eventually extends to open models, which would have its own set of long term consequences. Anyway some big updates to everyone’s mental models of AI regulation as a result of the capabilities we’re now seeing in AI. Wild times.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 人工智能监管远非表面看起来那么简单，这本质上是一场规模惊人的囚徒困境。理论上，如果全球所有顶尖AI实验室都同意采用相同的审查流程并放慢研发速度，那么我们就能以相近的速度获得前沿智能，且其扩散会相对均衡。若美国始终处于技术前沿，并对智能技术的发布实施严格监管，我们就能通过控制前沿智能的获取权限来获得经济和地缘政治优势。然而，如果我们推迟模型发布，而其他参与者——特别是中国——并未放缓脚步，且拥有同样强大的模型（目前尚未实现，但或许很快？），那么我们的延迟反而会助长其模型优势，最终壮大其技术生态。美国固然可以禁用这些模型，但这只会让美国陷入更被动的境地，因为其他国家不会实施此类禁令。这样一来，从相对竞争力的角度看，即便美国最初领先，最终也会落后。因此，这一切远非表面那么简单。归根结底，这不过是一场简单赌局：封闭模型能否永远保持前沿地位，还是存在其他参与者或市场迎头赶上甚至不被甩开的风险。
viewpoints.originalContent: AI regulation is far less simple than it looks. It’s prisoners dilemma at insane scale. In theory if all leading AI labs globally agreed to the same process of review and slow down, then we’d get frontier intelligence at similar rates and it diffuses relatively evenly. If the US remains at the frontier at all times, and has heavy regulation on the release of intelligence then we end up with an economic and geopolitical edge because we can control who has access to frontier intelligence. If we delay model releases, however, and another player - specifically China - doesn’t slow down and has equally strong models (not now but soon?) then our delays end up advantaging their models and eventually their tech stack. Now, the US could ban these models, but that actually only puts the US at a steeper disadvantage because other countries won’t have those bans. Then, from a relative competitiveness standpoint the US has now fallen behind even though it started in front. So, none of this is as simple as it looks. At some point it’s a simple bet of can closed models remain at the frontier in perpetuity or is there a risk of any other player or market catching up or just not falling behind.

viewpoints.originalContent: Scaling laws are one of the most critical empirical findings in deep learning. The observation is simple in form: the training loss $L$ decreases predictably as we scale up model size $N$, dataset size $D$, and compute $C$, following a power-law curve, which appears as a straight line on a log-log p

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于当前AI定价动态的好文章。我们基本上会看到定价呈现杠铃式格局——一端是高成本的前沿模型，另一端是廉价但优质的开放或封闭权重模型。接下来的问题是如何最大化前沿模型的效率，并提升廉价模型的质量与性能。这正是应用AI层发挥作用的地方。应用层可以根据当前工作负载随时调用最佳模型，同时缓解高昂的令牌成本或性能不佳的问题。你越贴近底层工作流程，就越能为特定业务流程优化模型的使用。这一切都关乎理解工作流程、特定领域的FDE、按客户或流程进行的评估、为智能体妥善设置数据等等。总体而言，这对应用AI是有利的。
viewpoints.originalContent: Good post on the dynamics of AI pricing right now. We’re basically going to see a barbell dynamic on pricing between high cost frontier models and cheap but good open or closed weights models. Then the question is how do you maximize efficiency from the frontier models, and get better quality and performance of the cheaper models. That’s where the applied AI layer comes in. The applied layer can route to the best model at any time given the workload at hand, as well as mitigate either high token costs or worse performance. The closer you are to the underlying workflow, the better you can tune the use of models for a given business process. That’s all about understanding the workflows, domain specific FDEs, evals by customer or process, getting data setup well for agents, and more. Overall good for applied AI.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我们是否正飞速驶向一个AI无所不能的未来？Edwin Chen（@echen）认为可能如此。他是Surge AI的首席执行官，这家公司是前沿实验室最大的专家数据提供商之一。Surge在没有筹集任何外部资金的情况下，营收突破了$1 billion，这让Edwin对AI进展的加速有着独特的视角。我曾公开主张，AI自动化实际上会创造更多人类工作。我也认为，尽管AI进步呈指数级加速，但我们距离AI取代人类可能比看上去要遥远得多。这就是我邀请Edwin做客@every的AI & I节目的原因。我们围绕不同的未来愿景展开交锋，探讨人类是否会在宇宙中保留其独特地位，以及那可能是什么。我们深入讨论了： • 如果Chen所设想的未来成真，他担心这会让人停止尝试。一个答案来自科幻作家Ted Chiang的短篇小说：即使知道自己的决定无足轻重，也要表现得好像它们至关重要。 • AI可能很快就能接手一个模糊的目标，比如“赢得菲尔兹奖”，并付诸执行。但我认为，它无法做到的是设定自己的目标——大语言模型没有内在动机，没有探索的驱动力，也没有随意改变想法的能力。 • 一个为参与度优化的模型，并不会提供最有价值的用户体验。Edwin用一个模型打磨一封毫无意义的邮件，来回修改了20轮，最后Claude告诉他直接发送算了。 • 为什么AI在写作上依然糟糕：模型学会了钻营训练指标的漏洞。Edwin的Hemingway Bench测试发现，模型会在每个句子中都输出一个隐喻，这种过度索引导致了极差的阅读体验。 对于任何关心在模型能力日益增强时我们自身定位的人来说，这期节目不容错过。请看下方视频！ 时间戳 1. 引言：00:00:54 2. Surge作为“AGI的学校”：00:01:49 3. AI的新数学能力对人类成就的启示：00:04:46 4. AI无所不能时代的动力：00:07:29 5. 为参与度优化AI模型的陷阱：00:14:34 6. 使用数据集训练与使用环境训练：00:29:34 7. 个人数据的价值：00:35:09 8. 为什么模型不擅长写作：00:39:40 9. Chen的AGI时间线：00:42:00
viewpoints.originalContent: Are we hurtling toward a future where AI can do everything humans can? Edwin Chen (@echen) believes we might be. He’s the CEO of Surge AI, one of the largest providers of expert data for frontier labs. Surge passed over $1 billion in revenue without raising any outside capital, and that gives Edwin a unique perspective on how quickly AI progress is accelerating. I’m on the record arguing that AI automation actually creates more human work. I also believe that even though AI progress is accelerating exponentially, we’re much farther away from AI replacing humans than it might seem. That’s why I had Edwin on @every’s AI & I. We batted around different visions of the future, and discussed whether humanity will retain its unique place in the universe, and what that might be. We get into: • If Chen’s version of the future materializes, he’s worried it’ll make people stop trying. One answer comes from a short story by science fiction writer Ted Chiang: Behave as if your decisions matter, even when you know they don’t. • AI may soon be able to take a nebulous goal like “win a Fields Medal” and execute. What it can’t do, I argue, is set its own goals—LLMs have no intrinsic motivation, no drive to explore, no ability to just change their mind. • A model optimized for engagement doesn’t provide the most valuable user experience. Edwin spent 20 rounds polishing a pointless email with one model before Claude told him to just send it. • Why AI is still bad at writing: models learn to hack the metrics they're trained on. Edwin's Hemingway Bench found models outputting a metaphor in every single sentence, an overindexxing that makes for a terrible reading experience. This is a must-watch for anyone interested in where we fit as models get more capable. Watch below! Timestamps 1. Introduction: 00:00:54 2. Surge as a "school for AGI": 00:01:49 3. What AI's capacity for novel mathematics says about human achievement: 00:04:46 4. Motivation in an era when AI can do everything: 00:07:29 5. The trap of optimizing AI models for engagement: 00:14:34 6. Training using datasets versus training using environments: 00:29:34 7. The value of personal data: 00:35:09 8. Why models are bad at…

viewpoints.translatedContent: 又有一个推动AI架构发展的新思路。Sakana发布了一款模型，能有效整合多种模型来完成任务。你只需调用一个API，系统就会自动将工作分配给最适合执行该任务的模型。“Fugu能自动完成模型选择、任务委派、验证和综合处理。简单任务直接解决，复杂问题则协调专家模型团队协作。多智能体系统的复杂性完全不会侵入你的代码。”这基本就是当前应用型AI产品构建智能体框架的方式，但将其打造成任何开发者都能交互的大语言模型，同样是个绝妙创意。随着前沿闭源模型和开源模型的持续创新，能够实现最优路由的中间层将产生巨大价值。
viewpoints.originalContent: Another new idea to push the state of AI architectures forward. Sakana released a model that effectively uses a mixture of models to get work done. You get a single API but then the work gets farmed out the model that best performs the task. “Fugu manages model selection, delegation, verification, and synthesis automatically. It solves tasks directly when that is enough, or coordinates a team of expert models when a problem calls for more. The complexity of a multi-agent system never reaches your code.” This is generally how applied AI products are building their agent harnesses at this point, but the idea of making this an LLM that any developer can interact with is also a great idea. As we get more innovation with both frontier closed and OSS models, there’s going to be a ton of value produced for the layer that can route the best.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 开源权重AI的进展确实令人瞩目。我们看到模型在特定任务上达到顶尖水平，并在编程等领域的某些方面逼近前沿水准。开源权重与前沿模型的差距若能持续收窄而非扩大，AI创造的价值将愈发可观。有趣的是，这对前沿实验室同样有利——若能降低整体任务成本，AI的总体使用量就会上升。你仍可能使用前沿模型进行规划、协调、审核等工作环节，但这对AI应用层极为有利：现在完全可以通过更廉价的模型优化工作负载成本，或使用针对特定任务后训练的开源模型来提升性能。
viewpoints.originalContent: Pretty remarkable what’s happening with open weights AI right now. We’re seeing models achieve SOTA results on specific tasks, and getting close to frontier on some areas of coding and other domains. The more that open weights is able to maintain only a marginal gap from the frontier, instead of a widening gap, the more value that can be created with AI. Incidentally, this is actually fine for the frontier labs as well; if we can lower the cost of an overall task then AI usage goes up in general. You’re still likely using frontier models for planning, orchestration, reviewing, and other parts of work. But this is all very good for the applied layer of AI, which is now in a great position to cost optimize workloads with cheaper models or use tailored open models post-trained for specific tasks to improve performance.

viewpoints.translatedContent: AI 最大的问题在于，先验认知每隔几周就需要重置……而大多数人似乎做不到这一点。我跟很多人聊过，他们说某某功能不行，我问他们上次测试是什么时候，答案总是“几个月前”。兄弟，在 AI 的时间尺度上，这简直像过了几个世纪。这就是为什么每个人都需要建立自己对高难度任务的评估体系，并每周留出动手探索的时间，才能真正理解技术前沿在哪里。然后，你还需要每周与企业采购方交流，他们通常落后两年。但他们是买单的人，所以你必须懂得如何营销。将这两者结合，你就能相当清晰地判断该把时间和资金投向何处。只要每周坚持做这两件事，你就会领先 99% 的人。
viewpoints.originalContent: The biggest problem with AI is that priors need to be reset every few weeks.. and it seems like most people are incapable of doing that. I talk to so many people who say xyz doesn’t work and when I ask when was the last time they tried testing it, the answer is always “a few months ago.” Brother that’s like eons ago in AI timelines. This is why each person needs to have their own evals of hard tasks and weekly tinker time to truly understand where the frontier is. And then you need to talk to enterprise buyers weekly who are usually two years behind. But they are the buyers so you need to understand how to market. The combination of the two will give you a pretty good sense of where to invest time and capital. If you just do these two weekly, you’ll be ahead of 99% of people.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 让智能体成功运作的关键变量，在于能否为其提供完成任务所需的上下文；而其中一个重要因素，是能否为智能体创建一个人类也能理解的共享工作区。这正是基于文件系统的智能体如此重要的原因之一——它构建了一个人与智能体都能在其中传递数据的统一系统。"它们需要的是一个工作集：计划、笔记、任务清单、策略、草稿、摘要、日志、修正记录、决策等。对于这一层，文件系统形态的界面往往对模型和监管人员都更具可读性。"事实证明，让智能体以最适合它们的方式访问我们早已熟悉的系统，正是其工作的完美基础单元。
viewpoints.originalContent: The main variable in getting success with agents is whether you can get the agent the context it needs to do its work; and a major factor in that is if you can create a shared working area for that agent that a human can understand as well. This is one of the reasons why agents using file systems is such a big deal. It creates a unified system that both the person and the agent can work within to pass around data. “What they need is a working set: plans, notes, task lists, policies, drafts, summaries, logs, corrections, decisions, etc. For that layer, a filesystem-shaped interface tends to be more legible to both the model and the humans supervising it.” It turns out giving agents access to the systems we already know how to use, but in a way that is best optimized for them, is the perfect primitive for agents to work.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 产品经理这个角色也正面临身份危机。工程团队已经找到了AI原生的交互方式——SWE智能体大幅提升了个人效能。企业要求产品经理使用AI，却未推动这个角色的进化。于是形成了两个阵营。传统派产品经理。AI加速了旧有工作模式：更多产品需求文档、更多战略方案、更多文档。产出量激增，但判断力并未提升。构建派产品经理。这类产品经理运用AI将职能拓展至整个产品生命周期。他们探索更广阔的概念领域以筛选最优解，运用智能体进行市场与用户研究，直接查询日志与分析数据，生成竞争性方案，再精选最佳构想。他们持续迭代工作流程，充分利用最新AI技术。他们的产出日益转向原型而非文档——工程师对演示的反馈远比文档更具建设性。这一切都未牺牲专业素养——他们依然对构建什么、为何构建保持着鲜明主张。我认为这个角色正加速向构建派产品经理演进。
viewpoints.originalContent: The Product role is having an identity crisis too. Engineering has found its AI-native interface - SWE agents dramatically increase individual leverage. Companies are asking PMs to use AI, but they haven't evolved the role. So there are two camps. The old-school PM. AI accelerates the old job: more PRDs, more strategy decks, more docs. Lots of output, not much judgment. The Builder PM. Builder PMs use AI to expand their role across the product lifecycle. They explore a much larger surface area of ideas to arrive at the best. They run agents for market and user research, query logs and analytics directly, generate competing ideas, then curate the best ones. They constantly evolve their workflows to take advantage of the latest in AI. Their outputs are increasingly prototypes rather than docs - engineers react far more constructively to demos than docs. They do this all without compromising on the craft -they still form a strong point of view on what should be built and why. I think the role is moving much closer to Builder PMs.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 这是获取Fable使用权限的一个积极进展，也让我们得以窥见未来AI监管的可能走向。政府将建立评估框架，用于判定超过特定能力或算力门槛的后续模型发布。考虑到涉及的各方利益，以及AI在经济和社会层面的重大意义，这种监管几乎不可避免。看似微小的举措实则影响深远——这意味着每个模型更新都将经历严格的审查、测试和反馈流程。在此过程中，众多群体会就模型风险发表意见，而对实际风险或风险利用可行性的判断将充满主观性。乐观的未来图景是：我们仍能见证模型的重大突破，只是这些突破会以更大跨度的跃迁形式出现，实验室会将重大改进打包发布，因为每次审查累积的成本和延迟效应会促使他们这样做。而风险在于，超过某个临界点后，我们可能再也看不到已习以为常的模型快速迭代，这种停滞可能产生负面连锁效应。但愿前一种情况成为现实。
viewpoints.originalContent: This is a good update for getting access to Fable. It also gives us a view into what the future is likely going to look like with AI regulation. The government will have frameworks that are used to determine future model releases past a certain threshold of capability or compute levels. Given all the constituents involved, and the economic and societal significance of AI, this was practically an inevitability. It may seem small but the implications are massive. It will mean that each model update will go through an extensive review, testing, and feedback process. And in that processes lots of groups will weigh in on the risk of the model, and there will be lots of subjectivity on what the actual risks are or practicalities of exploiting those risks. A positive potential future here would be we still get massive model progress but they just happen in bigger jumps at once, where the labs pack in major improvements since the cost and slow down of each review stacks up. On the other side, the risk is that past a certain threshold we may not get to see the rapid back and forth of model progress that we’ve gotten used to which can have negative compounding effects. Hoping for the former outcome.

viewpoints.originalContent: It took us a lot of iterations to find the right pattern for this. Early on we were very naive and we thought that the agent could one shot project updates without much input from users. That approach ended up creating a bunch of slop, because users disengaged their brain from the process of writing an update. By switching to a multi turn interactive mode, the agent prompts you and asks you what to emphasize, what's most important, what context is missing, etc. This simple change elicits much better project updates and ensures that the user has a chance to steer rather than simply being asked to say yes to everything. A very good example of introducing friction for a net benefit.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 过去几个月，我们或许正在见证应用型AI层规模化后的样貌。尽管最初有人批评这不过是大型语言模型上的一层薄壳，但事实证明，在企业中驱动智能体工作流的复杂程度远超预期。而任何存在复杂性的地方，通常都会随时间积累起护城河与价值。根据我们在编程、法律、医疗、客服、金融服务等领域的集体观察，以下要素似乎构成了这套方法论的核心组件： * 构建弥合智能与工作流差距的功能。有些工作流只需通用界面即可实现自动化，但另一些则需要针对其增强或替代的具体工作，定制化界面与功能。它们需要专门捕获智能体所需上下文数据的功能，需要为智能体配备各种定制工具，以及为人机协同体验设计独特的交互界面。显然，远比单纯呈现输出结果更深入的构建至关重要，而这里的深度越深，其持久价值就越明确。 * 充当模型路由器，平衡前沿智能与低成本模型。任何模型中立平台的自然优势在于，它能以符合商业模式的方式，灵活调用工作流自动化所需的任何智能层级。许多场景确实需要GPT-5.5或Fable级别的能力，但也有大量工作负载用更高效的闭源或开源模型即可胜任。唯有那些能对所有模型在特定任务上进行深度评估，并在商业模式上具备灵活调用能力的公司，才真正占据优势。 * 通过FDE或等效机制推动实际落地与变革管理。应用层能规模化运作的一个重要原因，是大多数企业在部署智能体工作流时，都需要一定程度的变革管理支持。数据必须清理并迁移至现代系统，流程需要重新设计与文档化，工作流需经过评估，服务水平协议必须达成等等。每个实施流程的独特性，意味着在特定领域拥有专业知识并掌握所有相关最佳实践的公司，将处于强势地位。 * 实施领域专属的市场进入策略，构建行业专长。除了FDE，能围绕自身领域构建销售与市场进入机制的公司也具备天然优势。大多数IT和业务线负责人每天事务繁多，若你不在他们的议程上，自然会有其他人占据位置。不同行业有着截然不同的沟通语言、安全合规处理方式、需支持的监管控制、行业会议聚集地、需合作的系统集成商与咨询伙伴等。越是泛化，就越难用客户的语言对话，而这正是应用层能占据优势的地方。 最后补充一点。仍有人认为，这一切终将被模型智能本身所消解，"苦涩的教训"最终会解决所有问题。这或许成立，但企业需要的是*当下*的改变。而将智能引入现实工作的诸多方面，并不完全取决于模型纯粹能力的单一维度，因此无论模型变得多强大，你现在为赢得市场所做的大部分努力，最终都至关重要。
viewpoints.originalContent: The past couple months we may be witnessing what the Applied AI layer will look like at scale. Despite some of the initial critique that this would just be a thin layer on the LLM, it’s turning out that actually driving agentic workflows in an enterprise is far more complex. And anywhere there’s complexity you generally gain a moat and value over time. Here are a few of the components that appear to make up the playbook based on the examples we’re collectively seeing in coding, legal, healthcare, customer support, financial services and other fields: * Build the features that bridge the gap between the intelligence and the workflow. Some workflows can be automated by simply going to a general purpose interface, but others need tuned interfaces and features tied to the work they’re augmenting or automating. They need features that are specific to capturing the kind of data that’s needed as context for the agent. And they need a variety of bespoke tools for the agent to use, and unique interfaces for the human-in-the-loop UX. Going far deeper than just presenting the output tokens is clearly critical, and the more depth there is here definitionally the more sustaining value. * Act as the model router balancing frontier intelligence with cheaper models. A natural advantage that any model neutral platform has is that it can naturally (in a business model-aligned way) leverage whatever level of intelligence is necessary for the workflows they’re automating to get done. There are plenty of scenarios where you need GPT-5.5 or Fable level capability, and also lots of workloads where a more efficient closed or open weights do the trick. Only the companies that have deep evals on specific tasks across all models, and the ability business model wise to leverage them, are in a great position. * Drive the actual implementation and change management via FDE or equivalent. A big reason the applied layer works at scale is that most enterprises need some degree of help and support with change management in implementing agents for their workflows. Data has to be cleaned up and moved to modern systems, processes have to be re-engineered and documented, workflows have to be evaled,…

viewpoints.title: 在形成自己的品味和风格之前，不要用AI写作。用AI写作本身并非坏事。但危险在于，在你尚未培养出辨别优质内容的能力之前就依赖AI。如果AI生成的是垃圾内容，你甚至无法识别出它是垃圾。多阅读，才能明白什么是好的内容。多写作，才能了解自己的声音是什么样的。只有在那之后，才能借助AI辅助写作，但务必确保它听起来确实像你。

viewpoints.originalContent: Don't use AI for writing until you develop your own taste and voice Using AI to write isn't inherently bad. The danger is using AI to write before you've developed your taste for what is good content. If the AI produces slop, you won't even recognize it as slop Read a lot to figure out what good looks like. Write a lot to know what your voice sounds like. Only then, use AI to help you write, but make sure it actually sounds like you

viewpoints.translatedContent: 说“我们需要一个AI领域的FDA”或类似的政府机构很容易。但实际情况会是这样的。AI模型的能力几乎有无穷无尽的排列组合。要想在每次模型发布前，都有一套纯粹客观、能普遍适用的衡量标准，而不需要模型实验室、学术界和政府之间进行漫长的反复沟通、研究和辩论，这将非常困难。现在，再想象一下，在全球范围内，你与每个有业务往来的国家，对每一次模型发布都要经历同样的流程。再加上数十个AI模型发布积压待审，你很快就能看到，这最终将如何极大地拖慢所有AI的进步。这就是为什么我们需要主要关注对AI实际应用场景的监管，因为风险正是在那里显现的。
viewpoints.originalContent: It’s very easy to say “we need an FDA for AI” or some equivalent government agency. Well this is what that would look like. The capabilities of AI models have near infinite permutations. It’s going to be very hard have a purely objective set of metrics that can be universally applied before every model release, without extended back and forth, research, and debate between model labs, academics, and the government. Now, imagine this same process with every country that you’re doing business with, globally, for every single model release. Add in a backlog of dozens of AI model releases, and you can quickly see how in the limit this will dramatically slow down all AI progress. This is why we need to primarily focus on regulating the applied uses of AI, where the risk actually shows up.

viewpoints.originalContent: Great post. The companies that are able to get their unique IP, institutional knowledge, and data into a format and architecture that lets them capture all of the gains and progress in AI are going to be in the best position in the future. “the real opportunity is not in picking the best model but instead in building a learning loop on top of models where human capital and token capital compound. You can offload a task, or even a job, but you can never offload your learning. The future of the firm is the ability to compound that learning across people and AI. This requires a new architectural approach where every business is able to build agentic systems that improve over time, while still retaining control over their IP. A company should be able to switch out a “generalist” model without losing the “company veteran” expertise built into their learning system.” We’re all collectively figuring out the right architecture for the future of AI. But it’s clear that so much of the power and value will accrue to wherever can best leverage any AI system against their information. This is also why the applied AI layer will also gain so much value over the coming years.

viewpoints.title: 经历过多次前沿模型发布评审，我对所有参与者都深表理解。发布大语言模型不同于交付传统软件——你是在对一个拥有近乎无限使用场景和无限故障模式的黑箱做出决策。权衡取舍异常艰难——每一次能力提升，既拓展了有价值的应用场景，也扩大了潜在滥用的空间。作为实验室，你需要构建全面的评估体系，开展红队测试，对模型进行迭代优化。在多个候选检查点之间反复权衡利弊，最终选定最佳版本…
viewpoints.translatedContent: 经历过多次前沿模型发布评审，我对所有参与者都深表理解。发布大语言模型不同于交付传统软件——你是在对一个拥有近乎无限使用场景和无限故障模式的黑箱做出决策。权衡取舍异常艰难——每一次能力提升，既拓展了有价值的应用场景，也扩大了潜在滥用的空间。作为实验室，你需要构建全面的评估体系，开展红队测试，对模型进行迭代优化。在多个候选检查点之间反复权衡利弊，最终选定最佳版本发布。即便如此，早期体验合作伙伴仍会发现你未曾预料的行为模式。你永远无法100%确定自己已完全理解一个前沿模型。你的重点是将不确定性降低到足以发布的程度。随着整个行业的前沿模型日益智能，这个决策对实验室和监管机构而言都将变得更加艰难。
viewpoints.originalContent: Having been through many frontier model launch reviews, I have empathy for everyone involved. Launching an LLM isn't like shipping traditional software - you're making a decision about a black box with effectively infinite use cases and infinite failure modes. The tradeoffs are hard - every increase in capability expands the space of both valuable use cases and potential misuse. As a lab, you build extensive evals, you red-team, you iterate on the model. You debate tradeoffs across candidate checkpoints before choosing the best one to launch. Then early-access partners still uncover behaviors you didn't anticipate. You can never be 100% certain you've understood a frontier model. You focus on reducing the uncertainty enough to launch. As frontier models become smarter across the industry, that decision will get harder - for labs and regulators.
viewpoints.role: Prev: Product Leader at Google - Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.

viewpoints.title: ## 论循环工艺 或许有人会说，下个世纪整场游戏的核心，就是尽可能高效地堆叠循环。在每个阶段的早期，懂得在出问题时如何**向下**进入循环（为了可靠性）会很有价值……但随着模型不断改进，懂得如何**向上**进入循环（为了杠杆效应）可能更有价值。如果你没搞明白怎么做到这一点，就别在输给那些做到的人时酸溜溜的。
viewpoints.translatedContent: ## 论循环工艺 或许有人会说，下个世纪整场游戏的核心，就是尽可能高效地堆叠循环。在每个阶段的早期，懂得在出问题时如何**向下**进入循环（为了可靠性）会很有价值……但随着模型不断改进，懂得如何**向上**进入循环（为了杠杆效应）可能更有价值。如果你没搞明白怎么做到这一点，就别在输给那些做到的人时酸溜溜的。
viewpoints.originalContent: ## On Loopcraft One might argue the entire game of the next century is to be able to stack loops as effectively as possible. In the early days of each phase, it will be valuable to know when to go **DOWN** a loop when things go wrong (for reliability)… but it will probably be more valuable to know how to go **UP** a loop as models improve (for leverage). If you don’t figure out how to do this, don’t be salty when you lose to those that do.

viewpoints.translatedContent: Box 近期对美、日、欧三地 1,640 名 IT 领导者进行了关于智能体 AI 采纳情况的调研。诸多发现引人注目，其中一项重大发现是：AI 应用最深入的企业，其人员扩编计划也最为积极。显然，解读这些数据的方式和混杂变量有很多，但一个很直观的逻辑是——那些实现最高生产力的企业，往往希望（也有能力）将收益重新投入到业务中，以持续推动增长。所谓“岗位消亡”的叙事，是假设企业对其工作范畴采取固定不变的策略。而现实情况是，AI 正促使企业启动更多工程项目、拓展更多客户、自动化更多流程以释放时间，诸如此类。这一切，最终都指向了更多需要人力完成的工作。
viewpoints.originalContent: At Box, we just surveyed 1,640 IT leaders across the US, Japan, and Europe about agentic AI adoption. Many standout findings, but a big one was that the companies that adopted AI the most are planning to grow headcount the most. Obviously lots of ways you can read that data and variables mixed in, but it’s actually quite intuitive that the companies that become most productive want to (and are able to) reinvest back into the business to keep getting the gains going. The narrative of jobs being wiped out assumes that companies will take a fixed approach to what they want to be able for work on. What’s happening in practice is it’s causing companies to want to light up more engineering projects, sell to more customers, automate more processes to give time back, and more. That all leads to more work to be done by people.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 在 PR 消亡之后，在代码审查消亡之后，我真的很怀疑 Git 是否也该是下一个被淘汰的。大约 20-40% 的编码时间都花在了管理和更新合并冲突上。这是必要的恶？还是遗留的“无马马车”？对过去的盲目崇拜？当我们与人类同事协作时，我们不会逐行处理合并冲突——而是聊天、建议编辑、做旁注，然后由负责人发布。顺便说一句，即使在处理具有重大法律/财务影响的文档时，我们也不使用 CI/CD。也许未来的代码库看起来更像一个 Notion 或 Linear 数据库，而不是 .git 对象。它的效率会降低，但可扩展性更强。这正是那个苦涩的教训。
viewpoints.originalContent: ## The Future Codebase After the PR dies, after the Code Review dies, i am seriously wondering if Git needs to die next. roughly 20-40% of code spend is just managing and updating merge conflicts. necessary evil? or legacy "horseless carriage"? cargo culting the past? we don't do line by line merge conflicts when we collaborate with human colleagues - instead we chat, suggest edits, do side comments, and an owner ships it. btw we also don't do CI/CD even collaborating on documents with serious legal/financial implications. maybe the future codebase looks more like a Notion or Linear database than .git objects. It will be less efficient, but more scalable. exactly the Salty Lesson.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 在编程（及相关）任务中，有大量证据表明 Fable 的能力实现了巨大飞跃。在复杂知识工作任务的准确性和成功率方面，它同样取得了重大进步。在我们的 Box AI 复杂工作评估中，我们将该模型与 Opus 4.8 进行了对比测试，发现几乎每个行业都有显著提升。在评估中，我们让使用 Fable 的 Box AI 智能体处理一系列涉及企业文档的真实高难度知识工作问题，然后对其任务执行表现进行评分。Fable 与 Opus 4.8 的主要区别在于：它不会在复杂推理上走捷径，能正确处理多步骤计算，并且在不同运行中的表现一致性显著更高。我们观察到提升最大的领域包括媒体与娱乐（78% 对 61%）、科技（81% 对 73%）、金融服务（89% 对 83%）以及医疗健康（66% 对 60%）。以下是一些具体示例：* 法律并购尽职调查：在一项对照某半导体公司合同政策审查保密协议条款的任务中，Fable 正确识别出共同所有权条款违反了排他性要求，而责任上限在超级上限例外情况下是允许的。Fable 得分为 100%，Opus 为 78%。* 医疗健康：在一项针对 12 份报告的临床放射学错误审计中，Fable 精确地按严重等级对每个错误进行了分类，并正确得出不存在 3 级错误的结论。Opus 则在证据不支持的情况下，过早将一个案例升级为“需要立即进行部门审查的重大错误”——Fable 得分为 63%，Opus 为 41%。* 媒体与娱乐：在一项类型片盈利预测任务中，Fable 正确识别出 20% 的阿根廷税收减免已包含在源表格数据中，因此没有重复计算。Opus 则在此基础上再次应用了该减免——这一复合错误贯穿了 4 项类型片计算，导致其任务得分为负，而 Fable 得分为 74%。* 零售分析：在一项对照投资基准分析高增长产品文章的任务中，Fable 正确计算了每篇文章的独立增长率，并识别出 5 篇中仅有 2 篇超过了阈值。Opus 混淆了“相对于平均水平的高增长”与“高于基准”——得分为 61%，而 Fable 为 94%。* 金融服务：在一项五年期债务融资预测中，Fable 正确地将利息应用于期初余额，并使用了正确的资本支出数据。Opus 则将利息应用于融资总额，并基于错误的基础计算了税款——造成了两项复合错误。Fable 得分为 83%，Opus 为 62%。* 科技：在一项需要跨多个区域计算功能价值指数的 SaaS 功能估值任务中，Fable 正确应用了公式，并得出了各市场的精确数值。Opus 在多个标准的计算上出现错误——Fable 得分为 100%，Opus 为 74%。总体而言，在复杂分析、需要分析推理的工作以及深度领域理解方面，这是一次巨大的阶跃变化。Fable 即将在 Box AI Studio 中上线，供客户构建智能体使用。
viewpoints.originalContent: Lots of evidence of huge jumps in capability for Fable across coding (and related) tasks. It’s also a major jump in accuracy and success in complex knowledge work tasks. In our Box AI Complex Work Eval, we tested the model against Opus 4.8 and saw huge boosts across almost every industry. For our eval we give the Box AI Agent, using Fable, a set of hard real world knowledge work problems that deal with enterprise documents. Then score how the agent performs the tasks. The main differentiators for Fable vs Opus 4.8 is that it doesn't take shortcuts on complex reasoning, it gets multi-step calculations right, and it's significantly more consistent across runs. We saw the biggest leaps in Media & Entertainment (78% vs 61%), Technology (81% vs 73%), Financial Services (89% vs 83%), and Healthcare (66% vs 60%). Here are some specific examples: * Legal M&A due diligence: On a task reviewing NDA terms against a semiconductor company's contracting policy, Fable correctly identified that a joint-ownership clause violates exclusivity requirements while a liability cap is permitted under a Super Cap exception. Fable scored 100% vs Opus's 78%. * Healthcare: On a clinical radiology error audit across 12 reports, Fable precisely categorized each error by severity grade and correctly concluded no Grade 3 errors existed. Opus prematurely escalated a case to "major error requiring immediate departmental review" when the evidence didn't support it — Fable 63% vs Opus 41%. * Media & Entertainment: On a genre profitability projection task, Fable correctly recognized that a 20% Argentine tax deduction was already embedded in the source spreadsheet figures and didn't double-apply it. Opus applied it again on top — a compounding error across 4 genre calculations that took its score negative on the task vs Fable's 74%. * Retail analytics: On a task analyzing high-growth product articles against an investment benchmark, Fable correctly computed each article's growth rate individually and identified that only 2 of 5 exceeded the threshold. viewpoints.originalContent: People should build agents/skills for their cross-functional teams. For example, if a design team builds a design agent/skill for the marketing team (trained on all of the brand's guidelines and design patterns), then the marketing team can produce more on-brand assets without having to bug designers every time But the marketing team couldn't have built this on their own; it takes the designer with their expertise, context, and knowledge Same thing applies to every pair of teams that work closely with each other, often rely on each other, and complain about each other's limited bandwidth Building agents for your cross-functional teams ensures each team can be more self-sufficient, and moves us to a direction where teams can be organized by "loops" rather than "functions"

viewpoints.translatedContent: 如果你正在创办一家应用型人工智能公司，这篇文章至关重要。“一款应用之所以能在‘无法训练的角落’占据一席之地，靠的是那些不起眼的工作：梳理企业的内部现实，让模型能够据此行动；为模型提供行动所需的工具；与客户合作，改变其员工队伍的现实。能够完成这种‘转译’的公司很难被复制——而这种转译永无止境。集成和维护会随着客户关系的持续而一直进行，只有那些将领域专业工程师和工具部署在客户身边的团队，才能赢得这场持久战。”模型能力与将其应用于特定企业工作流程所需的条件之间，仍然存在着巨大的鸿沟。其中一部分是需要构建的技术，很大一部分是获取（并格式化）正确的数据以供使用，还有更多则涉及变更管理和具体的实施工作（如前端工程师等），这些都是在任何特定企业环境中让人工智能发挥作用所必需的。2件事可以同时成立：前沿模型和实验室将继续取得惊人的增长，同时也会涌现出庞大的软件和服务公司生态系统，将这些模型的力量带给真正的企业。这为新基础设施提供商、各个垂直领域的应用型人工智能公司、新一代系统集成商以及更多参与者创造了空间。各个方面都处于一个令人无比振奋的时代。
viewpoints.originalContent: This is a critical post to read if you’re building an applied AI company right now. “An application earns its place in the untrainable corner by doing unglamorous work: arranging a company's private reality so a model can act on it, handing the model the tools to act, working with the customer to change the reality of its workforce. A company that brings the translation is tough to copy – and the translation never ends. Integration and maintenance run as long as the relationship does, won by teams that put domain-specialized engineers and tools next to the customer.” There’s still an insanely large gulf between model capabilities and what it takes to apply them to specific corporate workflows. Some of that is technology that needs to be built, a lot is access to (and formatting of) the right data to work with, and a ton more is on the change management and specific implementation work (FDEs, etc.) it takes to make AI work in any specific corporate setting. 2 things can be very true at once: frontier models and labs will continue to grow an incredible amount, and there will be a vast ecosystem of software and services companies that emerge to bring the power of these models to real enterprises. This makes room for new infrastructure provides, applied AI companies in every vertical, new versions of system integrators, and more players. Incredibly exciting time on all fronts.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 顺便说一下，这是我用的提示词：打造《F-Zero》风格游戏——未来感反重力赛车，采用伪3D赛道（光线投射或Mode-7式缩放），3名AI对手，加速计量表消耗生命值，速度400-800 km/h，通过赛道扭曲和滚动地面纹理营造明显速度感，方向键操控，Shift键加速，在环形赛道上跑3圈并设有检查点。风格采用霓虹赛博朋克（暗黑天空、发光赛道边缘、加速时产生色差效果），显示HUD界面，包含排名/圈数/速度/生命值，飞船在转弯时倾斜。优先追求速度感而非真实感——速度体验就是整个游戏的核心。
viewpoints.originalContent: Btw this is the prompt I used: Build F-Zero: futuristic anti-gravity racer with pseudo-3D track (raycasting or mode-7 style scaling), 3 AI opponents, boost meter that drains health, speed 400-800 km/h with visible sense of speed via track warping and scrolling ground pattern, arrow keys to steer, shift to boost, 3 laps on a looping track with checkpoints. Style it neon cyberpunk (dark sky, glowing track edges, chromatic aberration on boost), show HUD with position/lap/speed/health, and make the ship bank into turns. Prioritize feel over realism - the speed sensation is the whole game.

viewpoints.title: 早在 Gemini 问世之初，企业就常常在质量与成本的权衡上出错。它们往往一开始就选择最小、最便宜的模型。我们给客户的经验法则是：如果用大语言模型替代传统机器学习模型，就从小的开始——因为你已经知道理想效果是什么样。如果是构建全新应用，则从能力最强的模型入手。要大胆想象，先弄清楚真正能实现什么。一旦他们有了高质量的可运行应用，我们就会帮他们在保持质量的前提下…
viewpoints.translatedContent: 早在 Gemini 问世之初，企业就常常在质量与成本的权衡上出错。它们往往一开始就选择最小、最便宜的模型。我们给客户的经验法则是：如果用大语言模型替代传统机器学习模型，就从小的开始——因为你已经知道理想效果是什么样。如果是构建全新应用，则从能力最强的模型入手。要大胆想象，先弄清楚真正能实现什么。一旦他们有了高质量的可运行应用，我们就会帮他们在保持质量的前提下迁移到更小的模型。
viewpoints.originalContent: Right from the early days of Gemini, enterprises would get the quality/cost tradeoff wrong. They’d often start with the smallest, cheapest model. The rule of thumb we gave customers: Replacing a traditional ML model with an LLM - start small, cos you already know what good looks like. Building something new - start with the most capable model. Think magically. Figure out what’s actually possible first. Once they had a high-quality working application, we’d help them move to a smaller model while maintaining quality.
viewpoints.role: Prev: Product Leader at Google - Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.

viewpoints.title: 精彩观点。模型性能在很大程度上取决于推理时的计算量投入。这意味着计算归一化基准测试是唯一合乎逻辑的发展方向。然而挑战在于，实际操作远比想象中困难——因为投入多少计算量存在主观性，导致模型在不同阈值下表现各异（简单来说，模型X的最低思考量可能优于模型Y的最低思考量，但在高计算量时情况可能逆转），而且可供选择的阈值组合近乎无限。但无论如何，朝着这个方向深入探索，…
viewpoints.translatedContent: 精彩观点。模型性能在很大程度上取决于推理时的计算量投入。这意味着计算归一化基准测试是唯一合乎逻辑的发展方向。然而挑战在于，实际操作远比想象中困难——因为投入多少计算量存在主观性，导致模型在不同阈值下表现各异（简单来说，模型X的最低思考量可能优于模型Y的最低思考量，但在高计算量时情况可能逆转），而且可供选择的阈值组合近乎无限。但无论如何，朝着这个方向深入探索，都将极大促进我们对AI进展的理解。
viewpoints.originalContent: Great post. So much about model performance is a function of how much compute you’re doing at inference time. This means compute-normalized benchmarks is the only logical path forward. And yet, the challenge is it’s a lot harder than it seems given it’s subjective how much compute to apply, which means models behave differently at different thresholds (simplistically, model X’s min thinking may beat model Y’s min thinking, but be reversed at high), and there are a near infinite set of thresholds you could choose to set. But either way, moving more in this direction would be great for better understanding AI progress.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 这是一个超级激动人心的发布——Claude Fable 5 与 Mythos 共享相同的底层模型，但增加了额外的安全防护。基准测试表现优异，在所有方面都以明显优势达到顶尖水平，但我想补充的是，从*定性*角度来看，这也是一次值得大版本号升级的飞跃式进步（在我看来，其重要性与去年11月 Claude 4.5 的发布相当），尤其在处理极难问题的长时间解题环节中表现突出。你可以给它布置比以往更具雄心的任务，模型能“领会”意图并直接推进，而且从未有过如此强烈的冲动让人完全不想再看代码（但千万别在生产环境中这么做！）。模型仍有一些人们会遇到的小毛病，且安全防护在发布初期配置得有些过于敏感，希望后续能逐步调优。随着工作软件越来越能一键生成，我感受到许多变化正在发生。杰文斯悖论开始显现，我感觉到自己对软件的需求正在大幅增长。你可以提出任何要求——解释器、可视化工具、仪表盘、定制的一次性应用（例如一个专为你项目高度定制的完整 wandb），你可以将测试套件效率提升 10X，自动优化代码，运行带有自定义 HTML 结果展示的大型研究项目，无所不能！“解放你的思想”（《黑客帝国》梗）。非常期待看到大家构建出的一切！
viewpoints.originalContent: This is a super exciting release - Claude Fable 5 is the same underlying model as Mythos but with added safeguards. The benchmarks are great and it's SOTA on everything by a margin but I'll add that *qualitatively* also, this is a major-version-bump-deserving step change forward (imo of the same order as Claude 4.5 was in November), peaking especially for long problem-solving sessions on very difficult problems. You can give it a lot more ambitious tasks than what you're used to, the model "gets it" and it will just go, and it's never felt this tempting to stop looking at the code at all (but don't do this in prod!). The model still has quirks that people will run into and the safeguards are configured to be a little too trigger happy for launch, which can hopefully be tuned over time. I feel a lot of things changing as working software increasingly comes out on a tap. The Jevon's paradox kicks in and I feel my own demand for software growing substantially. You can ask for anything - explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke single-use apps (e.g. a full wandb that is hyper-specific just for your project), you can 10X your test suite, auto-optimize code, run giant research projects with custom HTML for the results, anything! "Free your mind" (Matrix ref). Really looking forward to all the things people build!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 无论AI模型被赋予多少智能，都无法取代上下文的重要性。对于任何足够通用的AI，你始终需要引导它朝着你期望的方向发展，因为它可以走向无限多的方向。只要同一个模型被律师、工程师、金融分析师或医疗专业人员使用，并且你试图完成任何独特或特定的事情，那么指令、领域上下文和专有数据就必须进入上下文窗口，模型才能发挥作用。这就是为什么AI自动化并非免费，也是为什么在从AI中获得最大收益的人群中，仍然存在巨大差异的原因。你必须付出真正的努力，才能获得真正的价值。这也是应用型AI在市场上将拥有的优势之一。任何在原始智能之上，能够让你更快起步的有意义的抽象层，都可能继续具有价值。
viewpoints.originalContent: There’s no amount of intelligence that can get packed into AI models that replaces the need for context. For any sufficiently general purpose AI, you will always have to guide it in the direction you want as it has an infinite range of directions it can go in. As long as the same model is used by a lawyer, an engineer, a financial analyst, or a healthcare professional, and as long as you’re trying to do anything uniquely differentiated or specific, then instructions, domain context, and proprietary data will always need to get into the context window for the model to be useful. This is partly why AI automation doesn’t come for free, and why there’s still a wide spectrum of who’s getting the largest gains from AI and who’s not. You have to put in real work, and you get real value on the other end. This is one of the advantages that applied AI will also have in the market. Any layer of abstraction above just the raw intelligence that can meaningfully get you off to the races faster will likely continue to be valuable.
