viewpoints.translatedContent: 我们已重置所有产品的使用限额！对于刚开始测试 Fable 的用户，这里有四条更高效使用的建议：1. 交给它比以往模型能处理的更大、更具挑战性的任务。2. 将 xhigh/high 努力级别设为默认以获得最佳性能，med 则用于更快的交互会话。3. 重新调整你的技能和 CLAUDE.mds。为先前模型编写的指令会让 Fable 固守旧模式，先让它自行判断。4. 从提供任务转向提供目标。描述完成后的状态及验证方式，然后让 Fable 自行探索路径（/loop 和 /goal 正是为此设计）。
viewpoints.originalContent: We've reset usage limits across our products! For those just starting to test Fable, here's four tips for using it more effectively: 1. Give it bigger, more ambitious tasks than what previous models could handle. 2. Use xhigh/high effort as your default for best performance, med for faster interactive sessions. 3. Rework your skills and CLAUDE.mds. Instructions written for prior models anchor Fable to stale patterns, let it use its own judgment first. 4. Move from providing tasks to providing objectives. Describe what done looks like and how to verify it, then let Fable find the path (/loop and /goal are built for this)

viewpoints.translatedContent: 这里的数字或许有些极端，但毫无疑问，在未来一两年内，不同模型系列之间的应用场景必将分层。我们将看到一种分化：面向高端任务和工作场景的前沿智能模型，以及针对海量工作负载、可充分剥离至低成本模型的廉价版本。前沿模型的规模仍将远超今日，因为应用场景会提出更高要求，但低端模型的市场也将大幅扩张。这里的关键更新在于，能够高效将工作负载路由至合适模型的那一层，将变得愈发珍贵，因为这将成为AI智能体领域新的难题之一。那些既能成功完成任务，又能实现成本优化的智能体编排系统，将占据强势地位。
viewpoints.originalContent: The numbers may be a bit extreme here, but unquestionably use-cases have to stratify in the next year or two between model families. We’ll see a split between frontier intelligence for high end tasks and work, and much cheaper models for high volume workloads that can sufficiently be peeled off to cheaper models. Frontier will still be far bigger than today because the use-cases will demand it, but the low-end will get quite a bit larger as well. The big update here is that the layer that can efficiently route the workload to the right model will then become increasingly valuable since that becomes one of the new hard problems in AI agents. Agent orchestration that can cost optimize while still performing the task successfully will be in a strong position.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 看到多项基准测试显示，Opus 是长时间运行任务的最佳模型。以下是让 Opus 自主运行数小时/数天的五个技巧： 1. 使用自动模式处理权限，这样 Claude 就不会请求批准 2. 使用动态工作流，让 Claude 协调数百/数千个代理来完成任务 3. 使用 /goal 或 /loop，推动 Claude 持续运行直至完成 4. 在云端使用 Claude Code，这样你可以合上笔记本电脑（最简单的方式是通过桌面或移动应用） 5. 确保 Claude 有办法端到端地自我验证其工作：通过 Chrome 浏览器扩展让 Claude 处理网页端，通过 iOS/Android 模拟 MCP 处理移动端，通过启动完整 Web 服务器或服务处理后端工作
viewpoints.originalContent: Seeing a number of benchmarks showing Opus is the best model for long-running work. Five tips for running Opus autonomously for hours/days: 1. Use auto mode for permissions, so Claude doesn’t ask for approval 2. Use dynamic workflows, to have Claude orchestrate hundreds/thousands of agents to get a task done 3. Use /goal or /loop, to nudge Claude to keep going until it’s done 4. Use Claude Code in the cloud, so you can close your laptop (easiest way is the desktop or mobile app) 5. Make sure Claude has a way to self-verify its work end to end: Claude in Chrome browser extension for web, iOS/Android sim MCP for mobile, a way to start the full web server or service for backend work

viewpoints.translatedContent: 这就是市场对AI吞噬企业软件的错误认知。过去打造优质软件极其困难。诚然，AI让这个过程变得稍微容易了些，但要构建出品味出众、差异化显著、品质卓越且安全可靠的软件，依然充满挑战。不过，这仅仅是打造企业级平台的一个环节。大多数企业软件公司的成本大头其实集中在市场推广上，因为规模化后，多数企业软件品类都难以突破，需要大量的咨询式销售，以及解决方案实施与集成的支持。AI并未减少这方面的需求，在许多情况下反而使其更为迫切——随着市场格局愈发纷繁复杂，采购方需要更专业的引导。当某个环节（软件开发）变得更廉价、更充裕时，新的难题——可发现性与市场差异化（市场推广）——就成了最难攻克的部分。
viewpoints.originalContent: This is what the market got wrong about AI eating enterprise software. Building good software in the past was very hard. Yes, AI has made that a bit easier, though it’s still hard to build something that’s got good taste, differentiated, high quality, secure, and so on. But nevertheless, that’s only one component of building a platform that enterprises rely on. The plurality of costs in most enterprise software companies is actually on GTM, because at scale most enterprise software categories are tough to break into and need a heavy amount of consultative selling and support for implementation and integration of solutions. AI hasn’t reduced the need for that, and in many cases requires it even more now, as landscapes get even more busy and complicated for buyers to navigate through. If you make one thing cheaper and more abundant (development of software) then the new problem of discoverability and market differentiation (GTM) becomes the hardest part.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 一种常见的误解是，认为训练数据工作技术含量低、纯属苦力活——无非是扫描些笔记本、从互联网上挖掘信息、创建标注样本。但推动模型前沿发展所需的数据恰恰相反。实验室需要的是针对高经济价值任务的训练数据。而在软件工程之外，这类任务大多缺乏文档记录——它们涉及复杂、特定领域的知识，是多年积累而成，横跨彼此不兼容的遗留工具。这就是为什么我们目前只有软件工程智能体，而尚未出现知识工作智能体的原因。像Mercor这样创建此类训练数据的公司，正在从事极具杠杆效应、高技术含量的工作。这对推动人工智能发展至关重要，却远未得到应有的重视。
viewpoints.originalContent: A common misconception is that training data is low skill, grunt work - scan some notebooks, mine the internet, create labeled samples. The data required to advance the model frontier is the opposite. Labs need training data for high-economic-value tasks. And most of these tasks outside of SWE have little documentation - it is complex, domain-specific knowledge built over the years, spanning legacy tools that don’t talk to each other. That's why we have SWE agents and not knowledge work agents yet. The companies creating this training data, such as Mercor, are doing extremely high-leverage, high-skill work. Critical to moving AI forward. And deeply underappreciated.

viewpoints.title: 比“始终使用计划模式”更聪明的做法是：始终将你的任务表述为一个问题，这样模型就会被引导去提出异议、评估想法的质量或建议替代方案，而不是盲目执行你所说的内容（这往往并非你真正想表达的意思）。实际上，只需在提示词末尾加上一个问号“？”，通常就能达到效果。

viewpoints.translatedContent: 代币成本正迅速成为我目前接触的所有企业最关注的话题之一。这对人工智能整体而言极为利好，因为它意味着这些系统的应用规模已超出此前预期。这也为应用型人工智能层开辟了另一种差异化竞争方向——模型路由。随着代币在任何工作流成本中占据显著比重，企业必然希望确保资金能最高效地用于特定任务的代币使用。前沿智能在编程、法律金融分析、医疗等高端任务领域始终不可或缺，相关投入只会持续增长。但同样地，你可以将单项任务剥离给成本更低的模型（无论是来自开放权重供应商还是主流实验室），从而获得更高效的最终成果。要实现这一目标，应用型人工智能层需要比任何人都更透彻地理解其领域内的工作流，并能针对不同任务灵活组合模型。若从事文档提取，你需要掌握各类文档类型中哪些模型表现更优或更差；若从事法律分析，则需了解哪些模型最擅长处理特定类型的任务，诸如此类。这将成为未来重要的差异化竞争点。那些拥有最佳评估体系、最强工作负载路由能力，且商业模式与客户财务目标高度契合的企业，将占据显著优势。
viewpoints.originalContent: Token costs are becoming one of the hottest topics for any enterprise I talk with right now. It’s very bullish for AI in general because it means these systems are being used at a scale that wasn’t contemplated before. It also gives way to another form of differentiation that will emerge for the applied AI layer, which is model routing. As tokens take on a significant amount of the cost of any given workflow, then companies will inevitably want to ensure that their dollars go into the most efficient use of tokens for the particular job at hand. Frontier intelligence will always be relevant at the high end of tasks, like coding, legal and financial analysis, healthcare, and more. And dollars spent here will only go up over time. But, equally, you can peel off individual tasks to lower cost models (whether they’re from open weights vendors or the major labs) and deliver a more efficient end outcome. To do this effectively, the applied AI layer needs to understand the workflows in their domain better than anyone else, and be able to mix and match models to different jobs. If you’re doing document extraction, you need to know which models perform better or worse for any given document type. If you’re legal analysis, you want to know which models perform various types of tasks best. And so on. This will become one of the bigger differentiation points over time. The companies with the best evals, the best ability to route the workloads, and those that have business models directly aligned to customers financial goals, will be in a great position.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 编程可以说是AI能够合理自动化的巅峰领域，然而我们仍然需要人类工程师监督智能体，才能让它们真正发挥作用。AI模型在海量复杂代码上接受训练，用户群体技术能力极强，能快速掌握最新工具。这项工作具有"可验证性"——因为你可以直接测试应用程序。成果质量往往与代码本身优劣脱钩（即便代码写得粗糙，应用仍能正常运行）。而智能体所需的上下文信息通常已经数字化并存在于代码库中。这些是AI编程智能体得天独厚的优势。其中部分优势也适用于知识型工作，但在需要全面审核才能产生价值、或数据数字化程度不高的领域，大多数优势并不存在。这使得知识型工作中的智能体面临更复杂的挑战。因此，即便在具备所有优势的编程领域，工程师需求依然旺盛，其他知识型工作领域的风险其实比人们想象的要小。智能体将让人们实现远超以往的产出，但人类本身并不会被取代。
viewpoints.originalContent: Coding is basically the pinnacle of what you could reasonably automate with AI, and yet we still need human engineers to oversee agents for them to be effective. The AI models are trained on an incredible amount of sophisticated code. The users are highly technical and can use the latest tools quickly. The work is “verifiable” because you can test an app. The outcomes are often removed from the quality of the code (you can have sloppy code but the app can still work). And the context for the agent is often already digitized and sitting in the codebase. That’s an incredible amount of benefits that AI coding agents get to work with. Some of those apply to knowledge work, but most don’t in areas where the work needs to be fully reviewed to be useful, or where data isn’t as abundantly digitized. This makes the job for agents in knowledge work more complicated. So if with all of that, engineers still remain in very high demand, the risks are going to be less than what’s perceived for other areas of knowledge work. Agents will let people do far more than they did before, but the people don’t go away.
